meetings.title: Durham City Council Work Session August 3, 2026
meetings.executive_summary: Presided over by Mayor Leonardo Williams in a makeup work session following the July recess (with Council Member Chelsea Cook noted as not yet present at roll call), the Durham City Council reviewed its 19-item agenda and pulled items 2, 6, 7, 8, 11, and 14 for discussion. During public comment and pulled-item review, residents raised noise-ordinance and traffic complaints regarding El Toro Loco, the former youth secretary of the Racial Equity Commission explained her resignation, and council members examined the forced repeal of the city's Equal Business Opportunity Program (EBOP) under Session Law 2026-41, emphasizing a shift toward contractor education while maintaining federal DBE/goals where federally required. Members also questioned recurring six-month amendments to the Turner & Townsend project management contract (paying 3.5% of project budgets versus 2% for in-house staff), reviewed holiday parade and Open Streets street closures, discussed accelerating neighborhood bike route and vertical-protection projects by defederalizing funding, and asked about public versus private lift stations. Council took two unopposed voice votes—approving an excused absence for Council Member Shanetta Burris for Thursday's work session and settling the evening agenda (consent items 1–16 and GBA public hearings items 17–19)—with no split or contested votes.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Roll Call, and Board Appointment Update
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Leonardo Williams called the August 3, 2026 makeup work session to order at 10:00 a.m. following the July recess, and the clerk called the roll with Williams, Javiera Caballero (called), Nate Baker, Shanetta Burris, Matt Kopac, and Carl Rist present (Williams noted he had not heard whether Chelsea Cook was attending). Council acknowledged budget implementation work ahead and received an appointment update noting R. H. Lenz was reappointed by a majority of council to the Durham City-County Environmental Affairs Board in the youth category.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda Review, Public Comment, and Racial Equity Commission Appointment (Item 2)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Williams read consent items 1–16 and evening public hearings 17–19, with items 2, 6, 7, 8, 11, and 14 pulled for discussion. During public comment, speakers addressed the unhoused population and neighborhood residents complained of 70–100+ decibel noise-ordinance violations (exceeding the 60-decibel limit), traffic issues, and site-plan compliance at El Toro Loco. On pulled item 2, former youth representative and secretary F. Yortojaguen explained her mid-term resignation from the Racial Equity Commission and questioned its capacity to fulfill its mission.

agenda_items.title: 2026 Appropriations Act (SL 2026-41) and Equal Business Opportunity Program Repeal (Item 6)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Pulled by Council Members Carl Rist and Matt Kopac, Deputy CFO Sheila Fawcett and the City Attorney briefed council on repealing the city's Equal Business Opportunity Program (EBOP) ordinance due to state legislation (Session Law 2026-41) eliminating minority- and women-owned business participation goals. Council members expressed disappointment following completion of a recent disparity study, and staff explained that while local goals are prohibited, the city can focus on contractor education and continue applying federal requirements on federally funded projects.

agenda_items.title: Fourth Amendment to Turner & Townsend Project Management Consulting Agreement (Item 7)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff explained that contracting with Turner & Townsend provides flexible project-management capacity for expanded project scopes and new July allocations at 3.5% of project budgets, compared with roughly 2% for fully loaded in-house staff salaries—a 1.5% cost differential that avoids putting capital projects on hold. Council members questioned returning for contract amendments every six months and asked staff to evaluate what project management functions can be handled in-house rather than continuing to expand consultant spending.

agenda_items.title: Street Closures for 2026 Movable City Open Streets and Durham Holiday Parade (Item 8)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Pulled by Council Member Matt Kopac and Mayor Leonardo Williams, Special Events Manager Kirk Archer with Parks and Recreation discussed coordination and funding for the 2026 Movable City Open Streets, the city tree lighting, and the 2026 Durham Holiday Parade. Members and staff discussed aligning partner events with Downtown Durham Inc. to activate the community downtown.

agenda_items.title: Bike Lane Vertical Protection and Neighborhood Bike Routes Construction Contract (Item 11)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Pulled by Council Members Nate Baker and Carl Rist, Assistant Transportation Director Bill Judge explained that bundling the two projects and defederalizing the neighborhood bike routes roughly 18 months earlier avoided NEPA and NCDOT review bottlenecks and accelerated delivery with more robust vertical protection. Baker asked about periodically closing high-use corridors to vehicles one day per week, while council members also discussed staffing constraints versus consulting contracts and anticipated benefits of the upcoming street design manual.

agenda_items.title: FY21 Lift Station Improvements Contract Amendment (Item 14), Excused Absence, and Agenda Settlement
agenda_items.discussion_summary: On pulled item 14 (Amendment 3 with Highfill Infrastructure Engineering PC), Council Member Carl Rist asked about the distinction between public and private lift stations in Durham, with staff noting very few private stations exist. Council Member Shanetta Burris then requested an excused absence for Thursday's work session due to travel, which council approved by voice vote before settling the evening agenda (consent items 1–16 and GBA public hearings 17–19) by voice vote and adjourning at 11:39 a.m.

meetings.title: Special City Council Meeting Nov. 16, 2026 at 5PM
meetings.presiding_chair: Mayor Pro Tem Patempo Lieto (Mayor running late; called to order by Mayor Pro Tem)
meetings.executive_summary: The Durham City Council held a special meeting on November 16, 2026, featuring a comprehensive presentation and discussion on the upcoming City Compensation Classification Study led by Gallagher consultants and HR Chief Erin Miley. The council reviewed market benchmarking methodologies, pay structure designs (step vs. open range), and strategies for mitigating wage compression. A significant portion of the meeting was devoted to a robust debate regarding the Durham Minimum Livable Wage (DMLW), its rent-based formula, projected increases exceeding $27/hour, and the resulting compression on lower-tier step plans, leading to a directive for staff to return with options and draft ordinance language.

agenda_items.title: Presentation on Compensation Classification Study and Durham Minimum Livable Wage (DMLW) Framework
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Erin Miley (Chief HR Officer) and Gallagher consultants Jamie Parker and Susie Parker presented the framework, methodology, and timeline for the City of Durham's upcoming Compensation Classification Study. The study aims to evaluate all job classifications, benchmark against comparator markets, address wage compression, and review compensation philosophy. Council members engaged in extensive discussion regarding timeline, compression challenges, and specifically the Durham Minimum Livable Wage (DMLW), which is projected to rise significantly under its current rent-based formula.
agenda_items.vote_summary: No formal vote was taken; council provided feedback and directed staff/city attorney to bring back options and draft ordinance/resolution language regarding DMLW adjustments and methodology for future budget cycles.

disagreements.meeting_title: Special City Council Meeting Nov. 16, 2026 at 5PM
disagreements.issue: Whether and how to adjust, pause, or reform the Durham Minimum Livable Wage (DMLW) calculation and implementation for the upcoming fiscal year to prevent severe wage compression.
disagreements.summary: Debate centered on balancing the progressive goals of the Durham Minimum Livable Wage with the severe wage compression and structural distortions it causes when out-pacing the rest of the compensation plan.
disagreements.side_a_position: Support a temporary pause/holding of DMLW at current levels while studying alternative methodologies to protect the pay plan from severe compression.
side_a_arguments: City Manager and HR administration argued that strictly following the current DMLW formula would push the wage above $27/hr, severely compressing the lower half of step plans and harming long-tenured employees unless massive additional funds are committed. Recommended exploring alternative calculation methodologies and holding the DMLW at the previous year's rate for one year as a pause/interim measure.
side_a_members: Manager Wanda Page (referenced/implied), Erin Miley, Mayor Pro Tem Patempo Lieto
disagreements.side_b_position: Cautious of pausing or lowering DMLW standards without careful study; preferred exploring structural alternatives without dismantling ordinance protections.
side_b_arguments: Several council members expressed strong attachment to the DMLW ordinance as a vital anti-poverty asset, voiced reluctance to 'chip away' or 'pause' it, and noted concerns about worker morale and trust, while acknowledging the severe budget and compression realities.
side_b_members: Council Member Rist, Council Member Cook, Council Member Burris
disagreements.resolution: No formal vote taken; council directed the City Attorney and administration to return with draft language and options (such as interim rates or alternative methodologies) for council review prior to budget deliberations.

agenda_items.vote_summary: Unanimous approval of Carle Tucker for the at-large seat on the Participatory Budgeting Steering Committee and Jacai Zippings for the youth category seat.

agenda_items.title: 2027 Federal Legislative Agenda
agenda_items.discussion_summary: City staff presented the FY 2027 federal legislative agenda, highlighting priorities such as minimum wage advocacy and federal assistance for environmental cleanup of contaminated soil in city parks and recreation spaces.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Placed on consent agenda for regular meeting.

agenda_items.title: Contract Amendment No. 1 for SW-103 Street Maintenance Repairs 2025
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council discussed street maintenance repairs and contracting under contract amendment number one for SW-103. Public comment raised concerns regarding local hiring practices and employment opportunities for local minority workers.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Pulled for discussion and moved to upcoming business.

agenda_items.title: FY 2027-28 Budget Development Schedule Amendment
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The City Manager presented a schedule adjustment for the FY 2027-28 budget development, rescheduling budget work sessions from May 26-27 to June 2-3, 2027.

agenda_items.title: Interlocal Agreement with Durham County for New Emergency Operations Center (EOC)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff presented an interlocal agreement with Durham County for the new Emergency Operations Center (EOC). Council members praised city-county administrative collaboration, renewable energy efficiency integrations, and discussed emergency medical service response times and 911 coordination.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Pulled for discussion and moved to upcoming business.

agenda_items.title: Commitment to DHA to Redevelop Tribute Rising (Forest Hills Heights)

agenda_items.vote_summary: Pulled for discussion and moved to upcoming business.

votes.item_title: Participatory Budgeting Steering Committee Appointments
votes.discussion_detail: The council considered board and commission appointments, specifically for the Participatory Budgeting Steering Committee. Following discussion, council members unanimously approved Carle Tucker for the at-large seat. meetings.title: Durham City Council November 2, 2026
meetings.executive_summary: The Durham City Council met on November 2, 2026, with Mayor Leonardo Williams presiding. The council discussed and approved several routine consent items, public appointments (such as L. Douglas Pender to the Durham Convention Bureau), US Department of Housing and Urban Development (HUD) grant agreements, water and sewer assessment rolls, and designated the Cranford-Wanamaker House as a local historic landmark. Additionally, the council debated and approved the annexation and utility extension agreement for 508 Olive Branch Road by a 6-1 vote, with Councilmember Baker voting in opposition due to revenue-negative concerns.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order & Roll Call
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Pro Tem presiding opened the meeting at 7:00 PM, followed by a moment of silent meditation and the Pledge of Allegiance led by Council Member Rist. The city clerk called the roll with Mayor Williams having an excused absence.

agenda_items.title: Ceremonial Proclamations & Recognitions
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Proclamations were read, including honoring Clyde Lindsey McPhatter Day (with remarks from Durham AARP Chapter 189 president Carver Joiner and family member Deborah McPhatter) and recognizing Team YL3C (youth-led center for public works careers).

agenda_items.title: Announcements by City Council Members
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council members shared announcements covering upcoming budget community conversations, tree canopy updates, condolences for city worker Lorenzo Wiley, gun violence reduction concerns, Native American Heritage Month, and urging residents to vote in the upcoming election.

agenda_items.title: Manager's Priority Items & Consent Agenda Adoption
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The City Manager presented priority items, and the council discussed items pulled from the consent agenda including the budget schedule and advisory board appointments.

agenda_items.title: Environmental Affairs Board Appointment
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Public comments were heard regarding the Durham City-County Environmental Affairs Board appointment, with several speakers expressing concerns over board recommendations and utility affiliations.

agenda_items.title: Eminent Domain for Sanitary Sewer Easement (1622 Crystal Creek Drive)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Public speakers and council members discussed eminent domain action to obtain a sanitary sewer easement at 1622 Crystal Creek Drive for the WS-862018 water and sewer extension project phase one.

agenda_items.title: Sunrock Camden Concrete Manufacturing Plant Major Special Use Permit & Site Plan
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The City Council conducted a quasi-judicial public hearing for a major special use permit and major site plan for the Sunrock Camden Concrete Manufacturing Plant (Application M2600001). Testimony was presented by city staff, the applicant's attorney and expert witnesses, and objectors regarding site design, traffic, property values, and a 10-year greenway easement condition.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Passed, 5-1 (Council Member Rist voted no on the permit; site plan passed unanimously)

votes.item_title: Appointment to Durham Convention Bureau (L. Douglas Pender)
votes.discussion_detail: The appointment of Jefferson S. Crawford to the Durham City County Environmental Affairs Board representing at large was brought forward for council consideration. Council Member Crook noted that while she did not personally know the applicant, she reviewed all applications and discussed the historical precedent of following board recommendations. Following discussion among council members regarding board recommendations and appointments, the matter was addressed, concluding the sequence of appointments.

votes.item_title: FY 2026-2027 US HUD Grant Agreement and Adoption
votes.discussion_detail: The FY 2026-2027 US HUD Grant Agreement and Adoption was processed as part of the council's legislative agenda items. Council members reviewed the administrative requirements associated with the federal grant funding and agreement. The item received full support and was adopted unanimously.

votes.item_title: Cranford-Wanamaker House Historic Landmark Designation
votes.discussion_detail: The Cranford-Wanamaker House Historic Landmark Designation was presented to the city council for official consideration and preservation review. Council members examined the historical significance and landmark status of the property under local ordinances. The designation motion was duly moved, voted upon, and passed unanimously.

votes.item_title: Annexation and Utility Extension Agreement for 508 Olive Branch Road
votes.discussion_detail: The annexation and utility extension agreement along with the associated permit and major site plan for 508 Olive Branch Road were brought before the council, featuring extensive discussion regarding operational buffers and greenway easements. Representatives from Sunrock, including Vice President Alex Culpepper, addressed council inquiries regarding the composition of the existing berm and recycled asphalt materials. Recommended conditions included maintaining plans substantially consistent with submissions and providing a 50-foot wide greenway easement along the north end of the parcel for the North Ellerbe Creek Trail that transfers to the city in fee simple after 10 years. The permit motion passed with a 6-1 vote, with Council Member Baker voting no, and the subsequent major site plan motion passed unanimously.

disagreements.meeting_title: Durham City Council November 2, 2026
disagreements.issue: Annexation and utility extension agreement for 508 Olive Branch Road (revenue-negative development vs. environmental benefits of city water/sewer connection).
disagreements.summary: Discussion on annexing 508 Olive Branch Road involving debate over revenue impact versus environmental benefits of city water and sewer connections.
disagreements.side_a_position: Support annexation and utility extension
side_a_arguments: Small negative revenue implication weighed against the huge environmental benefits of having homes on city water and sewer (avoiding failing septic tanks and phosphorus/nitrogen runoff into lakes).

side_b_arguments: Expressed concerns about revenue-negative development cases and consistency in rules and development plans.
disagreements.resolution: Passed 6-1 with Councilmember Baker voting nay.

meetings.title: Durham City Council October 19, 2026
meetings.executive_summary: The Durham City Council held its regular meeting on October 19, 2026, presided over by Mayor Leonardo Williams. The meeting opened with moments of silence for fallen firefighter Andrew Brooks and multiple ceremonial proclamations for National Diabetes Awareness Month, World Food Day, Domestic and Care Workers Day of Recognition, and Domestic Violence Awareness Month. The council subsequently held a public hearing and unanimously approved a local historic landmark designation for the Cranford-Wanamaker House at 1019 West Trinity Avenue. Finally, the council reviewed and approved a voluntary annexation, utility extension agreement, UDO zoning map change, and consistency statement for 508 Olive Branch Road, with the annexation passing 6-1 (Councilmember Baker voting no).

agenda_items.title: Opening, Moment of Silence, and Roll Call
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Meeting opened by Mayor Leonardo Williams with moments of silence including for fallen firefighter Andrew Brooks, followed by the Pledge of Allegiance and roll call.

agenda_items.title: Ceremonial Proclamations and Presentations
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Proclamations presented including National Diabetes Awareness Month, World Food Day, Domestic and Care Workers Day of Recognition, and Domestic Violence Awareness Month, with community speakers addressing council.

agenda_items.title: Council Member Announcements
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council members shared brief announcements covering community events, the funeral of firefighter Andrew Brooks, early voting updates, and city-county committee budget reports.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda Items
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Consent agenda items approved including assessment rolls for curb, gutter, paving, and water/sewer laterals on Chalmers Street and Link Street.

agenda_items.title: Appointment to Durham Convention & Visitors Bureau
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Appointment of L. Douglas Pender to the Durham Convention and Visitors Bureau / Tourism Authority.

agenda_items.title: HUD Annual Action Plan and Grant Agreement Authorization
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Adoption of the FY 2026-2027 US Department of Housing and Urban Development (HUD) Annual Action Plan and authorization of grant agreements.

agenda_items.title: Local Historic Landmark Designation for Cranford-Wannamaker House (1019 West Trinity Ave)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Public hearing and review of local historic landmark designation for the Cranford-Wannamaker House located at 1019 West Trinity Avenue, highlighting its architectural significance as a Queen Anne Shingle Style structure and historical association with Trinity College.

agenda_items.title: Voluntary Annexation and Utility Extension for 508 Olive Branch Road
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Public hearing and review of voluntary annexation, utility extension agreement, and UDO zoning map change for 508 Olive Branch Road (JC Construction LLC), with council discussion regarding road connections and revenue impacts.

agenda_items.title: Resolution on 2026 Constitutional Amendments Impact
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Resolution regarding the impact of 2026 constitutional amendments on Durham, discussing state constitutional amendment ballot measures and local fiscal/governance implications.

votes.item_title: Local Historic Landmark Designation for Cranford-Wanamaker House (1019 West Trinity Ave)
votes.notes: Passed unanimously after public hearing and presentation.
votes.discussion_detail: The Durham City Council considered a local historic landmark designation for the Cranford-Wanamaker House located at 1019 West Trinity Avenue. Public comments touched upon historic preservation merits, review processes, and potential tax revenue implications. Staff addressed council inquiries regarding why this landmark designation is the most fitting protection mechanism compared to other preservation options. Following discussion, the motion passed unanimously with no recorded opposition.

votes.item_title: Voluntary Annexation and Utility Extension Agreement for 508 Olive Branch Road (JC Construction LLC)
votes.notes: Passed 6-1 with Councilmember Baker voting no.
votes.discussion_detail: The City Council considered a voluntary annexation, utility extension agreement, and initial zoning map change for 0.462 acres located at 508 Olive Branch Road requested by Stuart Proctor LLC (JC Construction LLC) to connect a single-family home to water and sewer. Council member Baker raised questions regarding how Underbrush Drive terminates at the property and whether a through-connection or cul-de-sac was contemplated by prior development, with staff noting that transportation rules under the UDO do not require connecting the roads. Other council members supported the annexation, emphasizing the environmental benefits of connecting homes to municipal water and sewer to mitigate failing septic tanks and reduce phosphorus and nitrogen runoff into local lakes. The motion passed 6-1, with Council member Baker voting in opposition.

votes.item_title: UDO Zoning Map Change for 508 Olive Branch Road (Watershed Protection Overlay City Jurisdiction)
votes.discussion_detail: The Council considered a UDO zoning map change to remove 508 Olive Branch Road from the county jurisdiction of the residential rural Falls Jordan District B watershed protection overlay and establish the same under city jurisdiction. Following the discussion on the associated annexation and utility extension, the motion was duly moved, seconded, and passed unanimously.

votes.item_title: Consistency Statement for 508 Olive Branch Road per NCGS 160D-605
votes.discussion_detail: The Council considered the required consistency statement for the 508 Olive Branch Road annexation and zoning map change pursuant to North Carolina General Statute Section 160D-605. The statutory consistency statement was moved, seconded, and adopted by a unanimous vote.

meetings.title: Durham City Council Work Session October 8, 2026 (full meeting)
meetings.executive_summary: During the October 8, 2026 work session, the Durham City Council honored Digital Inclusion Week, observed a moment of silence and received updates regarding a tragic firefighter line-of-duty death, and reviewed the City Hall reconfiguration project contract. The council also discussed a proposed resolution regarding 2026 state constitutional amendments and engaged in a substantive policy debate regarding a proposed homeless encampment accountability policy.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Roll Call, and Excused Absences
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Pro Tem called the work session to order at 1:00 PM. The City Clerk called the roll, noting excused absences for Mayor Leonardo Williams and Council Member Reese. A motion was made and seconded to excuse Mayor Williams' absence, passing unanimously (5-0).
agenda_items.vote_summary: Passed, 5-0 (Motion to excuse Mayor Leonardo Williams' absence)

agenda_items.title: Line-of-Duty Death of Durham Firefighter & Emergency Services Update
agenda_items.discussion_summary: City Manager Wanda Page opened the meeting by sharing devastating news regarding the line-of-duty death of a Durham firefighter earlier that morning at 410 Marley Drive, along with two other firefighters injured. The Council held a moment of silence and expressed deep condolences and support to the firefighter's family, the Fire Department, 911 telecommunicators, and emergency services personnel.

agenda_items.title: Digital Inclusion Week Proclamation
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The Council proclaimed October 4th through 10th, 2026, as Digital Inclusion Week in Durham, honoring the city's Digital Equity Plan and collaboration with Digital Durham, Craden Institute, and local partners. Remarks were delivered by Patrice Carroll (Digital Inclusion Program Manager) and Jenna Bryant (Vice Chair of Digital Durham).

agenda_items.title: Introduction of UNC SOG Judith Wegner Fellow
agenda_items.discussion_summary: City Attorney provided a brief introduction of Lucas Lawrence, the first recipient of the newly founded Judith Wegner Fellowship in partnership with the UNC School of Government, placing a recent law school graduate in the City Attorney's Office for a year.

agenda_items.title: Durham Convention and Visitor Bureau Board Appointment
agenda_items.discussion_summary: City Clerk reported the appointment of L. Douglas Pender to the Durham Convention and Visitor Bureau (BCCT) for lodging and full services.

agenda_items.title: Public Comments
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Public comments were received from virtual and in-person speakers. Karen Boswell spoke regarding police department leadership and community safety concerns. Emily Sutton (Haw River Assembly) spoke against water connections for data centers (Project Lloyd) amid drought conditions and PFAS concerns.

agenda_items.title: Update on Environmental Remediation for Closed City Parks
agenda_items.discussion_summary: General Services and DPR staff presented an update on the environmental remediation and consulting contract (A1 and team) for the five closed city parks. Council members discussed budget allocations ($12 million CIP placeholder vs. $25M+ remediation estimates), state legislative assistance, and historical redlining impacts on industrial site locations.

agenda_items.title: City Hall Reconfiguration and Security Improvements Project Presentation
agenda_items.discussion_summary: John Potus Wilds (General Services) and Drew Tedman (Array Architects) presented the City Hall improvements project ($547,698 construction contract with Danielle Company LLC, total authorization $630,98) relocating Development Services to the first floor lobby, creating a security operations suite, family restroom, and lactation room, scheduled for January to March 2027.

agenda_items.title: Proposed Homeless Encampment Accountability Policy and Timing
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council Member Baker introduced the proposed Homeless Encampment Accountability Policy and Timing. Extensive debate ensued regarding the urgency of policy guidance, balancing compassionate outreach with state legislative pressures (House Bill 437), staff capacity, interim housing options, and potential subcommittee vs. staff-led processes.

votes.item_title: Motion to excuse Mayor Leonardo Williams absence
votes.notes: Unanimous voice vote among members present
votes.discussion_detail: At the beginning of the Durham City Council Work Session, the presiding officer noted that Mayor Leonardo Williams was absent and requested an excused absence for him. A council member promptly made a motion to excuse the Mayor's absence, which was duly seconded. The motion passed unanimously in a voice vote without any opposition.

disagreements.resolution: No vote taken; matter left for further discussion, consultation with the mayor, and review of staff implementation capacity.

meetings.title: Durham City Council October 5, 2026
meetings.executive_summary: The Durham City Council held its regular meeting on October 5, 2026, opening with ceremonial proclamations for National Disability Employment Awareness Month, Children's Health Equity Month, Energy Efficiency Day, and Hispanic Latino Heritage Month. The main legislative item discussed and voted upon was a zoning and annexation request for 3815 Wake Forest Highway, which sparked a robust debate regarding housing density, environmental impacts, infrastructure, and developer proffers. The council ultimately voted 4-3 to approve the annexation and utility extension, 4-3 to approve the UDO zoning amendment, and unanimously to adopt the consistency statement.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Roll Call, and Pledge of Allegiance
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Leonardo Williams called the Durham City Council regular meeting to order with a moment of silence. Council Member Carl Rist led the Pledge of Allegiance. Madam Clerk called the roll, confirming all council members present.

agenda_items.title: Ceremonial Proclamations and Performances
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The council presented several proclamations recognizing National Disability Employment Awareness Month, Children's Health Equity Month (Harper's Home), Energy Efficiency Day (Ashrae), and Hispanic Heritage Month, accompanied by community remarks and cultural performances.

agenda_items.title: Council Member Reports and Comments
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council members shared community updates, congratulated local events like Durham Pride and NCCU Homecoming, discussed intercity visits, and raised concerns regarding local violent crime, infrastructure, and housing affordability.

agenda_items.title: State and Federal Lobbying Services Contracts
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The council debated and voted on contracts for state and federal lobbying services, discussing the cost, effectiveness, and strategic necessity of retaining lobbying representation in Raleigh and Washington D.C.
agenda_items.vote_summary: State lobbying contract passed 4-3; Federal lobbying contract passed unanimously.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing & Action: 3815 Wake Forest Highway Annexation and UDO Zoning Map Amendment
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The council held a public hearing on a request for annexation, utility extension, and UDO zoning map amendment from rural/commercial to Planned Development Residential (PDR 18.4) for 3815 Wake Forest Highway to allow up to 200 apartments and townhomes. Extensive public comment and council debate focused on traffic congestion, stormwater/floodplain impacts, school capacity, and affordable housing proffers.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Passed 4-3 (Annexation & UDO amendment passed 4-3; Consistency statement passed unanimously)

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing: MIS Durham Headquarters 2 Annexation and Zoning
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Planning staff presented a request for voluntary annexation and direct translational Industrial Light zoning for approximately 9.8 acres located at 3429 Industrial Drive to connect to city utilities. Following staff presentation and public input, the council approved the annexation and zoning items unanimously.

votes.item_title: Annexation and Utility Extension Agreement for 3815 Wake Forest Highway
votes.discussion_detail: The motion proposed adopting an ordinance to annex 3815 Wake Forest Highway into the city of Durham and authorizing the city manager to enter into a utility extension agreement with a Court Holdings LLC. During the preceding discussion, council members debated developer costs, community benefits, and broader housing market pressures, with extensive focus on negotiated profers. Key developer commitments finalized during the debate included increasing affordable units from 5% to 8%, raising the Durham Public Schools (DPS) profer to $43,000, mandating 100% native trees, and modifying green building requirements (retaining Duke Hero while removing Green Guard, Green Globe, and Energy Star). Ultimately, the annexation and utility extension agreement passed on a 4–3 vote. Council members Baker, Burris, and Cook voted in opposition.

votes.item_title: UDO Zoning Map Amendment for 3815 Wake Forest Highway
votes.discussion_detail: The motion proposed adopting an ordinance amending the Unified Development Ordinance (UDO) to rezone the subject property at 3815 Wake Forest Highway from county jurisdiction (commercial neighborhood residential and residential suburban 20 within the Falls Jordan watershed overlay district B) to city jurisdiction as planned development residential 18.4 within the Falls Jordan watershed overlay district B. This zoning map amendment directly accompanied the annexation and utility extension agreement for the development site. Council debate leading into the vote covered the project's walkability, proximity to transit and commercial sites, and environmental considerations such as impervious surface limits set at 65%. The zoning map amendment passed by a 4–3 margin. Council members Baker, Burris, and Cook dissented.

votes.item_title: Consistency Statement for 3815 Wake Forest Highway
votes.discussion_detail: The motion proposed adopting the required statutory consistency statement under North Carolina General Statute section 160D-6005 for the 3815 Wake Forest Highway development actions. Following the votes on annexation and rezoning, the consistency statement was moved, seconded, and passed unanimously. No council members voted in opposition.

meetings.title: Durham City Council Meeting June 15, 2026
meetings.executive_summary: Presided over by Mayor Leonardo Williams with all seven council members present, the June 15, 2026 regular meeting featured opening discussion of an Indy Week report showing commercial property tax appeals removed $4.4 billion from tax rolls, Stage 2 drought restrictions effective that day, and priority items including law-enforcement technology rules and a data-center moratorium extension. In the recorded public-hearing actions, the council approved the Palmer Edge development tier change from Urban Tier to Suburban Tier on a 6-1 split vote—with Ayes from Leonardo Williams, Javiera Caballero, Nate Baker, Matt Kopac, Shanetta Burris, and Chelsea Cook, and Nay from Carl Rist after Rist argued suburban-style development is an inefficient use of land. Council then unanimously approved the accompanying Palmer Edge rezoning of roughly 50 acres from Residential Rural to Industrial Light (to unify the 185-acre former Glaxo campus assemblage) and its statutory consistency statement 7-0, and adopted comprehensive updates to Durham's minimum housing code (Chapter 10, Article 6) 7-0 before adjourning for the July break. (Note: the middle section of the source transcript digest covering consent and mid-meeting items was omitted.)

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Roll Call, Proclamations, and Council Announcements
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Leonardo Williams opened the meeting and Council Member Carl Rist led the Pledge of Allegiance, with all seven council members present at roll call. Council heard a Tourette syndrome awareness proclamation and announcements highlighting Durham Housing Authority's voucher transfer from Oxford Manor to Sandy Ridge Station, Pride Month, and Juneteenth. Multiple members underscored an Indy Week investigation detailing how $4.4 billion in property value—93% from commercial properties led by apartment buildings—came off the tax rolls via revaluation appeals, shifting tax burdens and straining future city budgets.

agenda_items.title: City Manager Priority Items, Stage 2 Drought Briefing, and Consent Agenda Reading
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The City Manager highlighted added materials for items 16, 22, 28, and 38, a revised resolution and memo for item 49 (law enforcement technologies), supplemental item 50 (Family Promise housing stabilization case management), and supplemental item 51 (public hearing extending a temporary moratorium on data centers and cryptocurrency mining facilities). Water Management Director Don Greeley briefed council on Stage 2 drought restrictions taking effect that day. Mayor Williams read the consent agenda, noting items 12, 14 (FY2026-27 budget and FY2027-32 CIP), 15, and 17 were pulled; subsequent mid-meeting discussion was truncated in the digest.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing: Palmer Edge Development Tier Change (Urban Tier to Suburban Tier) (Item 45)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Attorney Patrick Byker presented Palmer Edge's application to amend the development tier from Urban Tier to Suburban Tier to create an RTP-style campus with additional green space and proximity to NCCU, Durham Tech, and transit, noting unanimous Planning Commission support. Council Member Carl Rist questioned the shift and argued suburban-style development is not an efficient use of land. Council adopted the resolution amending the tier boundary by a 6-1 vote, with Rist dissenting.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing: Palmer Edge Zoning Map Change and Consistency Statement (Item 46)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff and applicant attorney Patrick Byker presented the rezoning of roughly 50+ acres north of Glover Road from Residential Rural to Industrial Light with a development plan, unifying an approximately 185-acre assemblage (including the former Glaxo campus already zoned Industrial Light) north to Ellis Road. Council Member Nate Baker inquired about Planning Commissioner comments on tree coverage, impervious surfaces, green infrastructure, and native plants, which Byker noted were too early in engineering to quantify. Council unanimously approved the zoning map change and adopted the N.C.G.S. § 160D-605 consistency statement 7-0.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing: Minimum Housing Code Amendments (Chapter 10, Article 6) (Item 48)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Assistant Director of Housing and Neighborhood Services Alexis John presented the first comprehensive update to Durham's minimum housing code since 2016, developed by benchmarking North Carolina peer municipalities alongside National Center for Healthy Housing and International Property Maintenance Code standards. The amendments clarify requirements, align with state statutes, and strengthen resident health, safety, and enforcement consistency. With no public speakers, council unanimously adopted the ordinance 7-0 and adjourned at 11:48 p.m.

meetings.title: Durham City Council September 17, 2026
meetings.executive_summary: The Durham City Council met on September 17, 2026, chaired by Mayor Pro Tem Caballero in the absence of Mayor Leonardo Williams. The council proclaimed World Alzheimer's Day, heard council member announcements addressing community safety and cultural heritage, approved an excused absence, and adopted the consent agenda unanimously. Additionally, the council appointed Mario M. Hayes to the Durham Housing Authority Board of Commissioners and unanimously adopted a resolution approving the Durham Cultural Roadmap following extensive public testimony from local artists and tribal representatives.

agenda_items.title: Announcements and Excused Absences
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council members shared announcements, including acknowledgements of recent community gun violence, upcoming holidays like Rosh Hashanah and Yom Kippur, the launch of the 'Keep It Durham Owned' economic initiative, and Hispanic Heritage Month reflections. Council Member Burris also requested and received an excused absence for the upcoming September 24 work session due to a trip to Kunshan, China.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Approved excused absence for Council Member Burris unanimously.

agenda_items.title: Priority Items and Departmental Updates
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The Acting City Manager, City Attorney, and City Clerk presented priority items, noting that certain items were postponed or referred back to staff. The Clerk also noted appointment statuses on General Business Agenda items.

agenda_items.title: Durham Housing Authority Board Appointment
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The council considered an appointment to the Durham Housing Authority Board of Commissioners. Mario M. Hayes was nominated and recommended for the position based on required financial and housing development experience.

agenda_items.title: Durham Workers' Rights Commission Appointment
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The Clerk noted that the Durham Workers' Rights Commission appointment had a split vote and a missing vote, and therefore would be re-advertised without taking action at this meeting.

agenda_items.title: Durham Cultural Roadmap Resolution and Public Hearing
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The council reviewed the Durham Cultural Roadmap and heard extensive public comments from artists, community members, and representatives of the Tuscarora Nation who requested historical acknowledgment and support for local grassroots artists. Speakers emphasized the need for affordable arts spaces, community-owned innovation hubs, and participatory budgeting. Following public comments, the council voted to adopt the resolution approving the Durham Cultural Roadmap.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Twenty-two routine administrative, operational, and financial items were presented on the consent agenda. No members of the public signed up to pull or speak on any consent items.

votes.item_title: Excused Absence for Council Member Burris
votes.discussion_detail: Council Member Burris requested an excused absence for the upcoming September 24th work session due to personal travel to Kunshan, China for a sister city celebration. The council discussed the scheduling and timing of her absence, noting it coincided with her birthday. A motion was made and seconded to approve the excused absence. The vote was conducted by the City Clerk and passed unanimously across all participating council members.

votes.item_title: Durham Housing Authority Board Appointment (Mario M. Hayes)
votes.discussion_detail: The council took up General Business Item 2 regarding an appointment to the Durham Housing Authority Board of Commissioners. Candidate Mario M. Hayes was nominated, meeting the criteria for a citizen with experience in financial statement analysis and housing development financing. A motion was made and seconded to appoint Mario M. Hayes to the board for a term expiring September 28, 2021 (noting transcript date references). The council voted unanimously to approve the appointment, expressing strong support for rigorous oversight and engagement with the Housing Authority.

votes.item_title: Durham Cultural Roadmap Resolution Adoption
votes.discussion_detail: The council considered Item 19, the Durham Cultural Roadmap, following a comprehensive public comment session featuring artists, cultural organizers, and members of the Tuscarora Nation. Public speakers highlighted the importance of supporting grassroots artists, providing affordable studio spaces, and recognizing indigenous history through markers. Council members praised the roadmap's potential to foster inclusive economic prosperity and cultural vibrancy in Durham. A motion was made and seconded to adopt the resolution approving the Durham Cultural Roadmap. The vote was conducted and passed unanimously among all council members present.

meetings.executive_summary: The Durham City Council held its work session on September 10, 2026, presiding in the absence of Mayor Williams. The manager also introduced new executive summary slides for future presentations and addressed inquiries regarding a private event at the Zafa Temple.

agenda_items.title: City Clerk's BCCT Report & Appointments
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The City Clerk presented board and commission appointment recommendations (BCCT report) for the Mayor's Hispanic Latino Committee, Durham Housing Authority Board of Commissioners, Durham Workers Rights Commission, and Durham Bicycle and Pedestrian Advisory Commission. agenda_items.title: General Public Comment
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Virtual and in-person speakers raised urgent public concerns regarding an unsanctioned homeless encampment near Fayetteville Street and Pilot Street adjacent to a public school, citing drug activity, public health issues, and safety hazards. agenda_items.title: Review & Settling of Consent & Departmental Items

agenda_items.title: Durham Cultural Road Map Presentation & Discussion

Council members expressed strong support, discussed equity, integration with other strategic frameworks, and scheduling the final resolution for the September 17 meeting.

agenda_items.title: 2026 Federal Legislative Update Presentation & Discussion
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Representatives from the Ferguson Group provided a comprehensive 2026 federal legislative update covering federal appropriations, earmarks, surface transportation reauthorization, HUD rulemaking, and municipal bond protections. agenda_items.title: Settling Agenda for September 17 Meeting & Meeting Adjournment

meetings.title: Durham City Council Meeting June 1, 2026
meetings.executive_summary: Presided over by Mayor Leonardo Williams, the June 1, 2026 Durham City Council meeting centered on the second public hearing for the proposed FY2026-27 budget and FY2027-32 Capital Improvement Plan amid what multiple council members described as an unprecedentedly tight fiscal cycle. In opening remarks, council members highlighted an Indy Week investigation detailing how commercial property revaluation appeals removed roughly $4.4 billion from Durham's tax rolls—93% from commercial properties led by apartment buildings—while Mayor Williams noted the hearing format meant council would listen without live back-and-forth. During the public hearing, residents, Legal Aid attorneys and paralegals, immigration-services nonprofits, and community advocates urged council to restore $191,000 in funding for the Durham Expunction and Restoration (DEAR) program, maintain eviction diversion and immigrant legal counsel funding, expand bus routes, protect lower-paid city workers' merit raises, and challenge corporate tax appeals rather than cutting social programs while funding police technologies. No formal votes or split votes are recorded in the available transcript digest (the middle portion of the digest was omitted prior to the closing of the public hearing and adjournment at 12:05 a.m.).

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Roll Call, and Council Opening Remarks on Budget and Property Revaluation
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Leonardo Williams called the meeting to order at 7:00 p.m., Council Member Carl Rist led the Pledge of Allegiance, and council members answered roll call and recognized Pride Month, Juneteenth, and Tulsa Race Massacre observance day. Members described the FY2026-27 budget as the toughest in recent memory, pointing to an Indy Week report that commercial property tax appeals—driven 93% by commercial properties and apartment complexes—removed over $4 billion from tax rolls and shifted burdens onto residents. Mayor Williams reminded attendees that the formal budget hearing is for listening and announced a follow-up Thursday budget work session at 9:00 a.m.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing on Proposed FY2026-27 Budget and FY2027-32 Capital Improvement Plan
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Following an omitted mid-meeting segment in the transcript digest, speakers testified during the budget public hearing on rental conditions, urged council to restore $191,000 in operational funding for Legal Aid's Durham Expunction and Restoration (DEAR) / Second Chance program, and requested sustained support for immigration legal services (Justice Matters, Church World Service, and World Relief). Other commenters opposed cutting eviction diversion, transit expansion, and community programs while criticizing an earlier vote on police technologies, urged restricting raises for higher-paid staff and officials while preserving merit raises for lower-paid workers, and called on the city to contest corporate property revaluation appeals before Mayor Williams closed the public hearing and adjourned at 12:05 a.m.

meetings.title: Durham City Council Work Session May 21, 2026
meetings.executive_summary: Presided over by Mayor Leonardo Williams (who noted at the outset that he needed to leave early), the May 21, 2026 Durham City Council work session reviewed a 37-item agenda covering homelessness strategy, economic development contracts, municipal election procedures, water quality enforcement, and a Museum of Durham History lease. Early in the meeting, council approved a closed session under N.C.G.S. § 143-318.11(a)(3) at the end of business for attorney-client consultation on pending litigation and an anticipated enforcement filing, heard public comments questioning HEART team funding on encampments and opposing pulling Parks and Recreation out of the West End Community Family Life and Recreation Center, and placed two board appointments lacking majorities onto the General Business Agenda. In the resumed afternoon portion, Water Management and City Attorney staff briefed council on the Brenntag stormwater pollution investigation, explaining why a $44,000 civil penalty was suspended pending compliance and prompting council questions about fine adequacy against a $17 billion corporation, state enforcement advocacy, and neighborhood outreach near Burton Elementary. Council settled the agenda (consent items 1–4, 7, 8, 10–25, 27–30, and 37; GBA items 5, 6, 9, and 26; and GBA public hearings 34–36) by unopposed voice vote before breaking into closed session, with no split votes recorded.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Priority Items, and Closed Session Motion
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Leonardo Williams opened the work session with Mayor Pro Tempore Caballero and Council Members Baker, Burris, Kopac, and Rist present at roll call, noting a heavy policy agenda and his need to leave early. The City Manager highlighted priority items including the Durham Strategic Framework to make homelessness rare and brief by 2031 (item 11), updated slides and a fact sheet for the municipal elections overview (item 31), and a supplemental lease with the Museum of Durham History at 521 West Morgan Street (item 37). Council approved a City Attorney motion by voice vote to hold a closed session at the end of business under N.C.G.S. § 143-318.11(a)(3) for litigation involving Isaac Woods, Jr., Cincinnati Insurance Company v. Lisa May Cranford, and an anticipated enforcement action.

agenda_items.title: Board Appointments, Consent Agenda Reading, and Public Comment
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The City Clerk reported nominations across seven boards and commissions, moving two appointments lacking a majority vote to the General Business Agenda. Mayor Williams read items 1–37 (noting item 26, Axon Enterprise renewal and expansion, was pulled with a speaker, alongside FY2025-26 budget amendments, stormwater and sewer vac trucks, Woodcroft Parkway design, one-hour free parking, Q3 financial report, FY2026-27 budget hearing, COCOLFRA incentive hearing, and Downtown Durham MSD contract). Public commenters questioned HEART team outcomes on unhoused encampments and protested any proposed budget withdrawal of Parks and Recreation from the West End Community Family Life and Recreation Center.

agenda_items.title: Water Quality Investigation Update: Brenntag Stormwater Enforcement (Item 32)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Following a truncated middle portion of the digest, Water Management staff reported on the multi-agency Brenntag creek contamination investigation led by the NC Division of Water Resources, noting a one-dimensional steady-state model was delayed while awaiting rain and creek flow. Staff explained that a $44,000 civil penalty (for prolonged reporting failures) was suspended in good faith while Brenntag completes administrative order requirements and noted collected civil penalties go to public schools by law. Council members questioned whether $50–$275 base penalties codified in 2006 deter a $17 billion global company, explored state-level advocacy with attorney Miles, and urged renewed door-to-door neighborhood outreach near Burton Elementary so children stay out of the creek.

agenda_items.title: Agenda Settlement and Recess to Closed Session
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff read the settled agenda placing items 1–4, 7, 8, 10–25, 27–30, and 37 on consent; items 5, 6, 9, and 26 on the General Business Agenda; and items 34–36 on GBA public hearings. Council approved settling the agenda by unopposed voice vote and took a 10-minute recess before entering the previously approved closed session.

votes.notes: Voice vote; mover, seconder, and individual member votes were not called by name in the transcript.

meetings.title: Durham City Council Work Session August 20, 2026
meetings.presiding_chair: Mayor Pro Tem Javiera Caballero (later Mayor Leonardo Williams)
meetings.executive_summary: The Durham City Council convened a work session discussing affordable housing development loan commitments, zoning and development items, department performance audits, and community priorities. The council reviewed departmental updates, discussed upcoming strategic plan milestones, and addressed public comments concerning housing affordability and municipal worker representation.

agenda_items.title: Closed Session Request & Staff Introduction
agenda_items.discussion_summary: City Attorney presented priority items including a request to go into closed session pursuant to NC General Statute 143-318.11(a)(3) for attorney-client consultation regarding two pending claims and (a)(6) to consider an interim clerk appointment, alongside introducing new litigation paralegal Ann Ross Pender.

agenda_items.title: City Clerk's Board Report & Commission Appointments
agenda_items.discussion_summary: City Clerk presented board reports and nominations for various commissions, including the Racial Equity Commission, Human Relations Commission, and Mayor's Council for Women.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda Reading & Pulled Items
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor and Council reviewed the consent agenda, pulling items 4, 6, 10, and 12 for separate discussion and deliberation.

agenda_items.title: Public Comment: Homeless Encampment & School Safety
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Public commenters, including Jacqueline Wagstaff, raised urgent concerns regarding homeless encampments near Fayetteville Street Elementary School ahead of the school opening, urging the council to provide flexible housing funds and wraparound services.

agenda_items.title: Public Comment: El Toro Loco Noise & Zoning Issues
agenda_items.discussion_summary: East Durham residents Ideal and Rachel Frier addressed unauthorized large-scale concerts and noise violations at El Toro Loco (311 South Plum Street), requesting city intervention and denial of temporary use permits.

agenda_items.title: Public Comment: Property Taxes & Traffic Safety
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Michael Harris expressed concerns regarding property tax hikes impacting seniors on fixed incomes and speeding issues along Highway 98 in the Oak Grove area.

agenda_items.title: Public Comment: City Council Expansion & Ward Representation
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Former council member/public speaker proposed a charter amendment to expand Durham City Council from seven to nine members by adding an at-large and a ward seat.

agenda_items.title: Community Violence Intervention Working Group Recommendations
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Presentation and discussion regarding community violence intervention (CVI) recommendations, working group findings, youth summits, and coordination across city, county, and community organizations.

agenda_items.title: Tenant Union Resolution & Housing Advocacy (Item 4)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Discussion on Item 4: Recognizing Ashton Seniors in Action and Willett Street United (WSU), and affirming the role of tenant unions in advancing safe, quality democratic housing. Council debated the scope of tenant resolutions versus broad policy statements.

agenda_items.title: Rockwood Cottages Loan Modification (Item 6)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Discussion on Item 6: Third loan modification agreement for Rockwood Cottages and Rockwood AH1 Limited Partnership, extending affordability through April 2030 and forgiving a portion of the city loan to preserve affordability for vulnerable seniors.

agenda_items.title: Reimagine Durham Freeway Study Report (Item 10)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Presentation and discussion on Item 10: Reimagine Durham Freeway study final report, exploring scenarios to reconnect communities divided by the highway corridor and repair historic harms.

agenda_items.title: 2026 Short Session Legislative Update (Item 15)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Presentation and discussion on Item 15: 2026 short session legislative update, covering state legislation, property tax caps, zoning reforms, and local advocacy.

agenda_items.title: Agenda Settlement & Motion to Hold Closed Session
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council settled the final agenda items and voted to proceed into closed session pursuant to state statutes.

votes.item_title: Approval of Meeting Minutes
votes.notes: Unanimous voice vote approving meeting minutes.
votes.discussion_detail: The assistant manager presented the settled agenda, noting that consent items included items 1 through 3, 5 through 14, and number 20, while GBA included item number 4 and GBA public hearings included items 16 through 19. A motion to settle the agenda was made, properly seconded, and passed unanimously with no opposition voiced.

votes.item_title: Motion to Hold Closed Session
votes.notes: Unanimous approval to hold closed session.
votes.discussion_detail: The city attorney requested a closed session pursuant to North Carolina General Statute 143-318.11(a)(3) for attorney-client consultation regarding two pending claims not yet filed, and pursuant to General Statute 143-318.11(a)(6) to consider an individual for appointment as interim clerk. A council member moved to approve the closed session following the language read by the city clerk, which was properly seconded and passed unanimously. Following the motion, the city attorney introduced Ann Ross Pender, the new litigation paralegal joining the office from Hartsog Law Group.

meetings.title: Durham City Council Work Session May 18, 2026
meetings.executive_summary: Opened and led through priority items, agenda reading, and public comment by Mayor Pro Tempore Javiera Caballero (with Mayor Leonardo Williams also participating later in the session), the May 18, 2026 work session reviewed a 23-item agenda and received three major staff presentations. Council pulled items 5, 6, 7, 14, 15, and 18 for discussion—covering involuntary commitment transportation, coordinated entry diversion, transportation projects including a two-way conversion, and Western Intake Partnership water facilities—while setting the FY2026-27 proposed budget presentation (item 2) for the evening business meeting. Water Management presented proposed FY2026-27 water and sewer rate increases of 12% (raising a typical household monthly bill from $80.08 to $89.75, with 14% projected out-year increases) and an update on the Goose Creek Outfall project, prompting discussion on expediting capital project delivery to avoid inflation-driven cost escalation. Community Partnerships and Engagement also presented post-storm home recovery tracking in Old Farm and River Forest alongside first-year neighborhood mini-grants and engagement programs, after which council settled the evening agenda by unopposed voice vote (consent items 1 and 3–19; GBA item 2; GBA public hearings 21–23) with no split votes.

agenda_items.title: Opening Remarks, Priority Items, Consent Agenda Reading, and Public Comment
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Pro Tempore Javiera Caballero led opening remarks—including Council Member Chelsea Cook's commendation of Parks and Recreation staff for the Bimbé Festival—and City Manager priority announcements for item 2 (FY2026-27 budget presentation scheduled for that evening), item 17 (water and sewer rates), and item 19 (Kimley-Horn Goose Creek Outfall contract). Caballero read items 1–23, noting items 5, 6, 7, 14, 15, and 18 were pulled and items 21–23 were public hearings. Public commenters spoke in support of the Vision Zero action plan and praised Parks and Recreation ahead of the June 1 budget hearing.

agenda_items.title: Proposed FY2026-27 Water and Sewer Rates Presentation (Item 17)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Following a truncated middle portion of the transcript digest, Water Management staff presented proposed 12% water and sewer rate increases for FY2026-27 (with 14% projected thereafter due to rising project costs), increasing a typical residential bill from $80.08 to $89.75 per month ($44.16 annually for tier-one customers) and commercial 5/8-inch accounts by $26 per month. Council asked about consumption trends and regional coordination. An audience member sought to comment off-agenda on HOME-ARP, CDBG, and ESG funding and was referred to city staff outside chambers.

agenda_items.title: Goose Creek Outfall Project Update (Item 19)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Water Management Director Don Greeley presented design, outreach, and construction schedule updates for the Goose Creek Outfall project, highlighting QR-code notifications for residents. Council discussion emphasized finding ways to expedite multi-year infrastructure delivery and add departmental capacity when needed so construction delays and inflation do not substantially increase overall project costs.

agenda_items.title: Post-Storm Recovery Update (Old Farm and River Forest) and Department Initiatives (Item 20)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: After a five-minute break, Community Partnerships and Engagement staff presented post-storm housing tracking across four statuses (repaired and returned, repairs in progress, not returned, unknown) for Old Farm and River Forest alongside first-year department milestones including the Hoover Road community cookout, Southern High School's participatory budgeting pilot (~$75,000 in community mini-grants), language access, ADA, and digital access efforts. Council members praised the staff's progress and discussed federal SBA relief limitations and stormwater-land use intersections.

agenda_items.title: Agenda Settlement and Adjournment
agenda_items.discussion_summary: City staff read the settled evening agenda incorporating work-session changes: consent items 1 and 3–19, GBA item 2, and GBA public hearings items 21–23. Council approved the motion to settle the agenda by unopposed voice vote and adjourned at 3:32 p.m.

meetings.title: Durham City Council August 17, 2026
meetings.executive_summary: The Durham City Council met on August 17, 2026, with Mayor Leonardo Williams presiding. The council heard announcements and proclamations, including a proclamation for Supportive Housing Week, received reports on the Unified Development Ordinance (UDO) Evaluation and Assessment Report, and considered various public hearings on curb, gutter, and paving assessment rolls. Notable actions included approving an excused absence for Council Member Shanetta Burris, confirming assessment rolls for Amber Place and Brunson Street, and continuing the public hearing and assessment roll confirmation for Lane Street to October 19, 2026, following resident objections regarding billing notice timelines and costs.

agenda_items.title: Opening & Roll Call
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Leonardo Williams called the meeting to order, followed by a moment of silence and the Pledge of Allegiance led by Council Member Rest. Roll call established a quorum with all council members present.

agenda_items.title: Proclamation: Supportive Housing Week
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Williams presented a proclamation recognizing August 24-28, 2026, as Supportive Housing Week in the city of Durham. Shante Addison, director of client services at Housing for New Hope, accepted the proclamation and shared remarks on collaborative supportive housing pathways involving local partners like Alliance Health, Duke School of Nursing, Freedom House, and StepUp Durham.

agenda_items.title: Announcements by Council
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council members shared opening announcements and community updates, including welcoming university students back to Durham, highlighting new leadership announcements, community events (such as the Durham Committee's 91st anniversary gala), and upcoming local initiatives and vigils.

agenda_items.title: Excused Absence - Council Member Shanetta Burris
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council considered an excused absence for Council Member Shanetta Burris for an upcoming Thursday session. A motion was made, seconded, and unanimously approved.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing: Comprehensive Plan & UDO Evaluation & Assessment Report
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Planning staff presented the annual evaluation and assessment report of the comprehensive plan and unified development ordinance (UDO) policy amendments, detailing revisions endorsed by JCCPC and approved by the BOCC. Public speakers raised concerns regarding public engagement, rural character protection (Policy 120), non-contiguous annexations (Policy 165), and UGB expansions (Policy 167/168).

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing & Assessment Role: Amber Place Paving
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff presented the assessment role for curb, gutter, and paving improvements to Amber Place from Humphrey Street to East Pedigree Street. With no public objections, council moved to adopt the confirmation resolution.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing & Assessment Role: Brunson Street Paving
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff presented the assessment role for ribbon paving constructed on Brunson Street from South Miami Boulevard west to the property line of Reid. Council adopted the confirmation resolution.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing & Assessment Roles: Chalmers Street Paving & Utilities
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff presented assessment roles for curb, gutter, paving, and water/sewer lateral improvements on Chalmers Street. Objections from specific property owners were noted, leading council to confirm the assessment role with exceptions for objecting properties and continue the hearing to October 19, 2026.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing & Assessment Roles: Lane Street Paving & Utilities
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff presented assessment roles for ribbon paving, water main, and sewer laterals constructed on Lane Street. Residents spoke during the public hearing expressing surprise and financial hardship regarding high assessment bills received years after project completion. Council discussed staff communication and voted to continue the item.

votes.item_title: Excused absence for Council Member Burrus
votes.discussion_detail: This routine procedural vote addressed an excused absence for Council Member Shanetta Burris. Council members and the mayor discussed council announcements, welcoming students back to Central and Duke, and community events such as supportive housing week. The motion passed unanimously with a 7-0 vote.

votes.item_title: Curb, Gutter, and Paving Assessment Role for Amber Place
votes.discussion_detail: This routine assessment role confirmation vote concerned curb, gutter, and paving improvements for Amber Place from Humphrey Street to North Humphrey Street North to East Pedigree Street. The transcript excerpt focused on comprehensive plan consistency reviews and policy tracking before the motion was moved, seconded, and passed unanimously (7-0).

votes.item_title: Ribbon Paving Assessment Role for Brunson Street
votes.discussion_detail: This routine assessment role confirmation vote addressed ribbon paving on Brunson Street from South Miami Boulevard west to the west property line of REID (Read 163690). Staff reported there were no objections to the assessment, and the council approved the resolution unanimously (7-0).

votes.item_title: Curb, Gutter, and Paving Assessment Role for Chalmers Street (Paving)
votes.discussion_detail: This vote concerned confirming the assessment role for curb, gutter, and paving improvements to Chalmers Street from Hemlock Avenue to the north property line of Reed REI 133231. Staff noted objections from certain property owners which were handled prior to the meeting and referred for further consideration on October 19, 2026, without requiring readvertising. The motion passed unanimously (7-0).

votes.item_title: Water and Sewer Lateral Assessment Role for Chalmers Street
votes.discussion_detail: This vote addressed the confirmation of the assessment role for water and sewer lateral improvements to Chalmers Street from Hemlock Avenue to the north property line of REI 133231. Following discussion on property owner objections and administrative procedures, the motion was moved, seconded, and passed unanimously (7-0).

meetings.title: Durham City Council Work Session August 6, 2026
meetings.executive_summary: The Durham City Council held a work session on August 6, 2026, discussing public comments on unhoused encampments (Oakwood Park) and tenant organizing at Ashton Apartments, transportation and infrastructure project agreements, a development loan commitment for 505 West Chapel Hill Street with Laurel Street Residential, and ongoing refinements to the multi-year strategic plan goals. The council also debated whether to intervene via resolution in private landlord-tenant disputes and whether to request an early presentation from the Durham Housing Authority regarding federal HUD default status.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Roll Call, and Announcements
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Call to order, roll call, and opening announcements by council members. Discussion regarding upcoming agenda items and meeting procedures.

agenda_items.title: Ashton & Willard Street Apartments Tenant Resolution
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council Member Baker proposed adding a resolution supporting tenant union collective bargaining at Ashton and Willard Street apartments to the next work session. Debate ensued regarding whether this is an appropriate role for city policy or a private landlord-tenant dispute.

agenda_items.title: Durham Housing Authority HUD Substantial Default Presentation Request
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council Member Cook requested a presentation from the Durham Housing Authority (DHA) regarding recent board decisions and HUD substantial default status. Council members debated the timing and appropriateness of summoning DHA prior to their fall update.

agenda_items.title: Public Comment on Housing, Tenants, and Encampments
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Public comments from residents and advocates regarding tenant unionization, living conditions, and safety at Ashton and Willard Street apartments, as well as concerns regarding unhoused encampments and park clearances.

agenda_items.title: Municipal Agreements and Transportation Project Updates
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff presentation and council discussion regarding municipal agreements for transportation and trail projects, including Third Fork Creek trail alignment changes, cost escalation, and federal funding tradeoffs.

agenda_items.title: Development Loan Commitment for 505 West Chapel Hill Street
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff presentation on the development loan commitment of up to $6.3 million with Laurel Street Residential for 80 affordable rental units at 505 West Chapel Hill Street, preserving future development options for the remainder of the site.

agenda_items.title: City Strategic Plan Update and Discussion
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Comprehensive review and discussion of the city strategic plan, including the number of goals, naming conventions, inclusion of bikeability, carbon reduction climate resilience goals, and initiative descriptions.

disagreements.meeting_title: Durham City Council Work Session August 6, 2026
disagreements.issue: Proposed resolution supporting tenant union collective bargaining at Ashton and Willard Street apartments
disagreements.summary: Debate over whether the City Council should adopt a resolution supporting tenant union collective bargaining for seniors at Ashton and Willard Street apartments.
disagreements.side_a_position: Opposed consideration of the tenant resolution as an improper role for city government
side_a_arguments: Argued that a city resolution is not the proper tool to intervene in a private landlord-tenant dispute and that local government should not dictate negotiation tactics.
disagreements.side_b_position: Supported placing the resolution on the work session agenda
side_b_arguments: Argued that the council has a duty to support tenants, provide transparency, and discuss protections for seniors facing lease burdens and retaliation.
disagreements.resolution: Agreed to place the resolution on a subsequent work session agenda to discuss both the resolution language and the proper role of local government.

disagreements.meeting_title: Durham City Council Work Session August 6, 2026
disagreements.issue: Requesting an early presentation from the Durham Housing Authority on HUD substantial default status
disagreements.summary: Debate on whether to require the Durham Housing Authority (DHA) to make an early presentation to the council regarding federal HUD substantial default status.
disagreements.side_a_position: Opposed early/special presentation request
side_a_arguments: Expressed concern that summoning DHA outside the scheduled annual update was viewed unfavorably as politically motivated criticism and that DHA staff were already hard at work responding to HUD.
disagreements.side_b_position: Supported scheduling an early informational presentation for transparency
side_b_arguments: Argued that public transparency and resident questions regarding HUD substantial default status necessitate an immediate informational presentation.
side_b_members: Council Member Cook, Council Member Baker
disagreements.resolution: No formal action taken; DHA to report back during its scheduled fall update.
