meetings.title: Durham City Council May 18, 2026
meetings.executive_summary: The Durham City Council met on May 18, 2026, opening with ceremonial proclamations honoring Clinical Trials Day, Huntington's Disease Awareness Month, National Public Works Week, and award-winning transit system GoDurham. The City Manager presented the proposed FY 2026-2027 budget and FY 2027-2032 capital improvement plan. The council debated and unanimously voted down an annexation and utility extension request for 4802 Cheek Road located outside the urban growth boundary (UGB). Finally, the council reviewed and unanimously approved annexation, utility extension, zoning map changes, and a consistency statement for the Sharon Road Assemblage project.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Pledge of Allegiance, and Roll Call
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Leonardo Williams called the meeting to order, followed by a moment of silence and the Pledge of Allegiance led by Council Member Rist. The city clerk conducted the roll call, confirming all council members present.

agenda_items.title: Ceremonial Proclamations and Recognitions
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The mayor and council presented ceremonial proclamations honoring Clinical Trials Day (accepted by Linda Schostek and local medical institution representatives), Huntington's Disease Awareness Month (accepted by Betsy McFarland and Dr. Burton Scott), National Public Works Week (accepted by Director Marvin Williams), and GoDurham Transit System of the Year Award (accepted by Director Sean Egan and transit partners).

agenda_items.title: Council Member and Manager Announcements
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council members shared community updates, including congratulations on anniversaries and graduations, upcoming budget public hearings, reflections on national and state legislative issues such as voting rights and right-to-work laws, and community grief over gun violence losses.

agenda_items.title: Manager's Priority Items: Proposed Budget & CIP Presentation
agenda_items.discussion_summary: City Manager presented priority items including the proposed Fiscal Year 2026-27 budget and FY 2027-32 Capital Improvement Plan (CIP), highlighting key investments and upcoming budget hearings, as well as an update on the Involuntary Commitment Transportation Plan Agreement.

agenda_items.title: Administrative and Consent Agenda Review
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The mayor and council reviewed administrative consent items, pulling specific items for separate comment and noting upcoming public hearing dates for the budget.

agenda_items.title: Consolidated Annexation and Rezoning for 4802 Cheek Road
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The council held a public hearing on the consolidated annexation and rezoning request for 4802 Cheek Road (Item 21), a proposed residential development outside the Urban Growth Boundary (UGB). Numerous residents and preservation advocates spoke against the project citing UGB violation, environmental and stormwater impacts on Triassic basin soils, lack of infrastructure (fire/EMS), and traffic, while the applicant defended the project's housing and environmental commitments. Following debate, the council voted unanimously to deny the annexation and utility extension.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Failed, 0-7 (Moved/Seconded; unanimous dissenting vote against annexation and utility extension)

agenda_items.title: Biannual Evaluation and Assessment Report (EAR) of Comprehensive Plan
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Planning staff presented the first biannual Evaluation and Assessment Report (EAR) of the Comprehensive Plan, covering proposed Place Type Map changes and UGB adjustments across three separate proposals (Treyburn Corporate Park parcels, a city-acquired lift station site, and a South Alston Avenue parcel). Council discussed the implications of each proposal, public transparency regarding UGB changes, and consistency with comprehensive plan growth policies.

agenda_items.title: Sharon Road Assemblage Annexation, Zoning, and Utility Extension
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The council held a public hearing and deliberation on the Sharon Road Assemblage annexation, utility extension, UDO zoning map change, and consistency statement (Item 23 part / Sharon Road). Residents raised concerns about traffic congestion, safety, and environmental buffers, while the applicant and council discussed increased proffers for affordable housing (8% at 60% AMI plus 2% at 100% AMI) and school contributions ($82,000). The council ultimately approved the annexation, utility extension, zoning change, and consistency statement unanimously.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Passed, 7-0 (Unanimous approval across annexation/utility extension, UDO zoning map change, and consistency statement)

votes.item_title: Consolidated Annexation 4802 Cheek Road (Item 21)
votes.notes: Failed unanimously following public comments regarding rural preservation, environmental concerns, and infrastructure/emergency service limitations outside the UGB.
votes.discussion_detail: The City Council considered a motion to adopt an ordinance annexing 4802 Cheek Road and to authorize a utility extension agreement with Horizon Land Group LLC. Council members expressed strong opposition, criticizing the proposal as poor planning and highlighting its inconsistency with the comprehensive plan. It was noted that both the planning commission and the county commission spoke forcefully against the project because it is located outside the urban growth boundary (UGB). Council members also raised concerns regarding the negative impacts of large corporate real estate developers on the area. Consequently, the motion failed unanimously in a 0-7 vote.

votes.item_title: Sharon Road Assemblage Annexation & Utility Extension (Item 23)
votes.notes: Passed following developer proffers increasing affordable housing and school contributions.
votes.discussion_detail: The City Council considered a petition from Noel Gosch with Morning Star Law Group for the voluntary annexation and utility extension of two parcels totaling 11.31 acres located at 1921, 2007, and 2013 Sharon Road, developed by Middleburg Development LLC. Discussion focused on negotiated proffers, including increasing income-restricted affordable housing to 8% at 60% AMI and adding 2% at 100% AMI for a 30-year period, as well as raising the Durham Public Schools contribution to $82,000. Council members expressed support for the project's housing strategy and growth within the UGB. The motion to adopt the annexation ordinance and utility extension agreement passed unanimously 7-0.

votes.item_title: Sharon Road Assemblage UDO Zoning Map Change
votes.discussion_detail: The City Council voted to amend the unified development ordinance for the Sharon Road Assemblage, changing the property jurisdiction and zoning from county classifications (industrial light, residential suburban 20, residential rural Falls Jordan Watershed Overlay District B) to city jurisdiction classifications (planned development residential 34.426, commercial general with development plan Falls Jordan Watershed Overlay District B). The motion was moved, seconded, and passed unanimously in a 7-0 vote.

votes.item_title: Sharon Road Assemblage Consistency Statement
votes.discussion_detail: The City Council voted to adopt a consistency statement for the Sharon Road Assemblage zoning map change, as required by North Carolina General Statute Section 160D-605. The motion to confirm consistency was moved, seconded, and passed unanimously in a 7-0 vote.

meetings.title: Durham City Council Work Session May 18, 2026
meetings.executive_summary: The Durham City Council held a meeting on August 24, 2026 (incorporating policy items and public hearings), where they discussed ceremonial items, consent items, and major planning and zoning matters. The council approved several routine items and held a detailed debate on Comprehensive Plan Amendment A25002 regarding evaluation assessment report policy changes, ultimately passing it 4-3 after striking commentary from policy 165. They also addressed zoning map changes and assessment roll confirmations.

agenda_items.title: Council Member Announcements & Community Events
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council members shared announcements and community updates, including highlights from the successful Bimbe Festival run by DPR, the Homegrown Hero Award presented to Kewon Hester, and attendance at the National Adaptation Forum and Bike Month events.

agenda_items.title: City Manager and Department Priority Items Review
agenda_items.discussion_summary: City management and department heads outlined priority items for the meeting and evening business session, highlighting the FY 2026-27 proposed budget, CIP, proposed water and sewer rates, and the Goose Creek Outfall engineering contract.

agenda_items.title: General Public Comment Period
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Members of the public addressed the council regarding community safety funding, youth mentoring models, Vision Zero land use reforms, and public park and recreation programming support.

agenda_items.title: Review of Administrative Consent & Departmental Items
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The Mayor Pro Tem and City Clerk reviewed administrative consent items, departmental items, presentations, and public hearings scheduled for the evening, pulling specific items for further discussion.

agenda_items.title: FY 2026-27 Proposed Water and Sewer Rates Presentation
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Don Greeley from Water Management presented the proposed water and sewer rates for FY 2026-27 and 10-year financial model, highlighting rate objectives, affordability programs, capital improvement spending for Jordan Lake and regulatory compliance, and household bill impacts.

agenda_items.title: City of Durham Involuntary Commitment Transportation Plan Agreement
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Community Safety Director Ryan Smith and staff presented the resolution adopting the City of Durham Involuntary Commitment Transportation Plan Agreement, enabling certified first examiners and HART teams to conduct first exams in the community and provide alternative transport. Council members questioned criteria consistency, unmarked vehicle availability, and operational metrics.

agenda_items.title: Coordinated Entry with Diversion Services Contract
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff presented the contract with Volunteers of America of the Carolinas Inc. for coordinated entry with diversion services. Council discussed why an RFP was not utilized immediately and noted upcoming HUD application schedules and provider capacity.

agenda_items.title: Utility Preliminary Engineering Construction Agreement (Tanaka Pkwy & Red Mill Rd)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff discussed the utility preliminary engineering construction agreement for Tanaka Parkway and Red Mill Road (TIP HE-0007B) involving NCDOT intersection improvements and roundabout installation. Council explored utility relocation cost burdens on local government and coordination with NCDOT.

agenda_items.title: Goose Creek Outfall Project Update & Professional Engineering Contract
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Don Greeley provided an update on the Goose Creek Outfall Project and letter to industry development restrictions, reviewing developer inquiries, outreach meetings, design/construction schedules, and acceleration strategies including early construction packages for interstate bores.

agenda_items.title: Post-Storm Recovery Update (Old Farm & River Forest Neighborhoods)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff from Community Partnerships and Engagement provided a post-storm recovery update for the Old Farm and River Forest neighborhoods following Tropical Storm Chantal, reviewing flood impacts, door-to-door outreach, financial and process barriers, and resilience planning.

agenda_items.title: Council Announcements, Meeting Schedule Review & Agenda Settlement
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council discussed scheduling conflicts for the September 21 meeting overlapping with Yom Kippur, reviewed administrative details, settled the evening's agenda, and adjourned the work session.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Passed via voice vote (unanimous motion to settle agenda)

votes.item_title: Comprehensive Plan Amendment A25002 Policy Changes
votes.discussion_detail: During the Durham City Council work session, the council considered procedural and agenda settlement items, including Comprehensive Plan Amendment A25002 policy changes and agenda adjustments for upcoming sessions. Council discussion preceding the vote touched on departmental efficiencies, neighborhood outreach programs, and scheduling adjustments for holidays such as Yom Kippur. The motion to approve and settle the agenda ultimately passed with a 4-3 vote. Nays were recorded by Nate Baker, Burris, and Cook, reflecting contested viewpoints on specific administrative or procedural matters during the session.

meetings.title: Proposed Budget for Fiscal Year 2026-27 presented on May 18, 2026
meetings.executive_summary: Opening the May 18, 2026 special City Council meeting, Mayor Leonardo Williams emphasized that Council would strictly receive the manager's budget presentation with no votes or debate until upcoming work sessions and the June 1 public hearing. City Manager Bo Ferguson presented an unprecedented $766.1 million FY 2026-27 proposed budget featuring a $326.0 million General Fund—a $489,000 year-over-year decrease driven by over 10,000 countywide revaluation appeals reducing the tax base by ~$2.6 billion and requiring ~$5 million in General Fund ($9 million all-funds) refunds. Despite constrained revenues, the proposal holds the property tax rate flat at 43.71 cents per $100, raises water/sewer rates 12%, funds 2% pay-scale raises and a $25.09/hour livable wage (while omitting merit/step increases), commits $4.55 million toward a $13 million homelessness response, continues fare-free GoDurham via an $8.2 million County Transit transfer, closes Forest Hills Pool early, pauses standalone speed humps, cuts $927,000 in outside agency funding, and lays out a $798.4 million 10-year CIP.

agenda_items.title: Opening Remarks and Procedural Scope
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Leonardo Williams opened the session by clarifying that Council would take no votes or policy action on May 18 and would reserve formal comments and deliberation for budget work sessions and the June 1 public hearing.

agenda_items.title: FY 2026-27 Proposed Budget Presentation: Revenue Reset, Taxes, and Workforce Compensation
agenda_items.discussion_summary: City Manager Bo Ferguson detailed how over 10,000 commercial and residential property tax appeals shrunk Durham's assessed base by ~$2.6 billion, producing Durham's first General Fund revenue contraction in recent memory ($326.0M vs $766.1M total budget) while still preserving AAA bond ratings via $2.2M fund balance usage and holding the tax rate flat at 43.71 cents ($1,853 median home tax bill). Water/sewer rates rise 12%, while employees receive 2% structural pay-scale raises, a 14% jump in the livable wage to $25.09/hour, absorbed health/dental increases, and a compensation study—balanced by suspending merit/step increases and eliminating 9 positions (4 vacant, 5 transitions) alongside 59 added or repurposed roles.

agenda_items.title: Public Safety, Reimagined Homelessness Strategy, and Fare-Free Transit Investments
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Ferguson highlighted funding for 16 firefighter positions for delayed Ladder Company 8 activation, firefighter cancer screenings, and overtime, alongside a $4.55M City commitment in federal/ARPA interest funds toward a $13M Year-1 community homelessness plan ($9M rental assistance) targeting 30% unsheltered and 50% youth homelessness reductions plus $725K eviction diversion and $100K emergency home repairs. GoDurham fare-free service continues for one year through an $8.2M one-time Durham County Transit Plan contribution.

agenda_items.title: Service Reductions, $798.4M Capital Improvement Program (CIP), and Adoption Calendar
agenda_items.discussion_summary: To balance constrained operating revenues, the proposal closes Forest Hills Pool permanently before summer 2026, limits new speed humps to street resurfacing projects, and reduces or eliminates $927,000 in outside partner agency funding while maintaining a $798.4M 10-year CIP prioritizing Connect Durham paving/sidewalks, Jordan Lake Water Treatment Facility, PFAS upgrades, an Emergency Operations Center, and a Southeast Durham fire station. Mayor Williams closed by calling the budget 'an impossible deck of cards' ahead of May 27-28 work sessions and the June 1 public hearing.

meetings.title: Durham City Council May 4, 2026
meetings.presiding_chair: Leonardo Caballero (Mayor Pro Tem) / Leonardo Williams (Mayor)
meetings.executive_summary: The Durham City Council held its regular meeting on May 4, 2026, issuing multiple ceremonial proclamations (Drinking Water Week, Taiwanese American Heritage Week, International Firefighters Day, and National Bike Month) and approving consent agenda items. The council adopted a 60-day temporary moratorium on data centers and cryptocurrency mining operations, approved economic development incentive agreements for AMAC Properties ($150,000) and CocoFro LLC ($115,000) along legacy commercial corridors, approved a consolidated annexation on South Miami Boulevard, and approved the consolidated annexation and rezoning (PDR 5.006) for the Enclave at Little Creek development with 20% affordable housing in a 4-2 split vote.

agenda_items.title: Ceremonial Proclamations and Council Announcements
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Pro Tem Caballero called the meeting to order, followed by a moment of silent meditation and the Pledge of Allegiance. Council received ceremonial proclamations for Drinking Water Week, Taiwanese American Heritage Week, International Firefighters Day, and National Bike Month, along with council member announcements and staff priority items.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda Approval
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The council reviewed and approved the consent agenda, which included performance audits, opioid settlement spending, HVAC upgrades, annual reports for Keep Durham Beautiful and Go Durham, budget amendments, and utility/infrastructure contracts.

agenda_items.title: Resolution to Set Public Hearing for Data Center Moratorium
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council took up a supplemental resolution to set a public hearing for a temporary moratorium on development approvals for data centers and cryptocurrency mining operations in the City of Durham.

agenda_items.title: Children's Wealth Building and Endangered Species Day Resolutions
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Public comment and ceremonial resolutions regarding Children's Wealth Building (savings accounts) and Endangered Species Day.

agenda_items.title: Temporary Moratorium on Data Centers and Crypto Mining
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Extensive public hearing and deliberation on imposing a temporary 60-day moratorium on development approvals for data centers and crypto mining operations. Numerous residents and advocates spoke on environmental, water, and energy grid impacts.

agenda_items.title: Economic Development Agreement - AMAC Properties, Inc.
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff presentation and public hearing on an economic development incentive agreement with AMAC Properties, Inc. for the renovation of Marzella's Professional Complex at 2919 Fayetteville Street ($150,000 city funding).

agenda_items.title: Economic Development Agreement - CocoFro LLC
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff presentation and public hearing on an economic development incentive agreement with CocoFro LLC for a freeze-dried ice cream production facility and tasting room at 1004 Morning Glory Avenue ($115,000 city funding).

agenda_items.title: Consolidated Annexation - 1418 South Miami Boulevard
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Public hearing on the consolidated voluntary annexation, utility extension agreement, and zoning consistency for two parcels totaling 3.44 acres at 1404 and 1418 South Miami Boulevard.

agenda_items.title: Consolidated Annexation & Rezoning - Enclave at Little Creek
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Major public hearing and contentious debate on the consolidated voluntary annexation, utility extension agreement, and rezoning (PDR 5.006 and RS-20) for 47.85 acres at 5524 and 5515 George King Road (Enclave at Little Creek) to allow up to 230 residential units with 20% affordable housing.

agenda_items.title: Revision to 2026 City Council Meeting Schedule
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Review and approval of supplemental agenda item to revise the 2026 City Council meeting schedule, rescheduling the May 7th work session to May 18th, 2026.

votes.item_title: Resolution to Set Public Hearing for Data Center Moratorium (Item 28)
votes.notes: Sets public hearing for temporary moratorium on data centers and crypto mining.
votes.discussion_detail: The council considered a resolution and associated procedural items to set a public hearing regarding a data center moratorium and related annexation and rezoning petitions. Discussions touched upon public hearing procedures, speaking time limits, and presentation materials from legal representatives such as Nil Ghosh regarding site constraints, natural heritage designations, and utility lift station infrastructure costs. Council members engaged in procedural management of public comments and meeting timelines. The motion was moved by Council Member Baker and seconded by Council Member Kopac, passing unanimously.

votes.item_title: Temporary Moratorium on Data Centers and Crypto Mining (Item 4)
votes.discussion_detail: The council considered an ordinance to adopt a temporary 60-day moratorium on development approvals for data centers, cryptocurrency mining operations, and associated processing facilities within the City of Durham pursuant to NCGS 160D-107. Council members discussed the lack of federal or state guidance and noted potential adverse impacts such as loud humming machinery near residential homes, low job creation, and poor land use compared to supporting local small businesses. Mayor Pro Tem Caballero and Mayor Williams highlighted regional organizing efforts and broader state-level legislative concerns regarding county water and grid usage. Following discussion, Council Member Rist moved and Council Member Burris seconded the motion to adopt the ordinance. The motion passed unanimously with no dissenting votes recorded.

votes.item_title: Economic Development Agreement - AMAC Properties, Inc. (Item 20)
votes.notes: Neighborhood revitalization grant for 2919 Fayetteville Street renovation.
votes.discussion_detail: The council evaluated an economic development agreement authorizing the city manager to execute a contract with AMAC Properties, Inc. in an amount not to exceed $150,000 for building renovations at 2919 Fayetteville Street. Speakers and council members emphasized supporting legacy businesses and small business ecosystems along the Fayetteville Street corridor, noting the property's five-decade history and its role as a microeconomic business hub and incubator. Council members Rist, Kopac, and Mayor Williams expressed support for neighborhood revitalization and local investment that avoids displacement. The motion was moved by Mayor Williams, seconded by Council Member Burris, and passed unanimously.

votes.item_title: Consolidated Annexation - 1418 South Miami Boulevard (Item 25)
votes.notes: Voluntary annexation of 3.44 acres with direct translational zoning.
votes.discussion_detail: The council considered a consolidated annexation and utility extension request for 1418 South Miami Boulevard, involving property annexation, zoning amendments from county to city jurisdiction for commercial general residential suburban-20 Falls/Jordan Watershed Overlay District B, and adoption of a consistency statement pursuant to NCGS 160D-605. Representatives for the property owner explained that the parcels are on the market and that neighborhood meetings had been held. Council members and staff reviewed satellite annexation policies, utility connections, and unified development ordinance standards. The motions were moved by Mayor Williams and Rist, seconded by Rist and Kopac, and passed unanimously across all votes.

votes.item_title: Consolidated Annexation & UEA - Enclave at Little Creek (Item 23) - Annexation & UEA
votes.notes: Annexation of 47.85 acres at 5524 and 5515 George King Road.
votes.discussion_detail: This motion proposed adopting an ordinance annexing the Enclave at Little Creek into the city of Durham and authorizing the city manager to enter into a utility extension agreement with Adobe Communities Acquisitions LLC. Council members debated the trade-offs of large-scale development, affordability components, and environmental conservation, referencing prior votes on Vision Zero, the comprehensive plan, and transportation planning. Council Member Caballero supported the case largely due to its high affordability component and lack of city subsidy. Conversely, dissenting members Nate Baker and Carl R. Burris opposed the motion, reflecting ongoing concerns regarding walkability standards, urban form, and the departure from desired growth patterns prior to the formal adoption of the LDC. The motion ultimately passed with a 4-2 vote, with Council Members Baker and Burris voting no.

votes.item_title: Consolidated Annexation - Enclave at Little Creek (Item 23) - UDO PDR 5.006 Amendment
votes.notes: Rezoning to PDR 5.006 for up to 230 residential units with 20% affordable housing.
votes.discussion_detail: This motion proposed amending the unified development ordinance to take property out of the residential suburban-20 Falls/Jordan Watershed Overlay B county jurisdiction and establish it as planned development residential 5.006 Falls/Jordan Watershed Overlay B city jurisdiction for the Enclave at Little Creek project. The discussion preceding the vote touched on balancing density, walkability, affordability, and environmental protections. Supporters emphasized the lack of city subsidies and the inclusion of strong affordability elements, while opponents maintained consistency with their positions on managing forested and large-scale properties. The motion passed 4-2, with Nate Baker and Carl R. Burris voting in the negative.

votes.item_title: Consolidated Annexation - Enclave at Little Creek (Item 23) - UDO RS-20 Amendment
votes.notes: Translational zoning for the second parcel to city RS-20.
votes.discussion_detail: This motion proposed amending the unified development ordinance to take property out of the residential suburban-20 Falls/Jordan Watershed Overlay B county jurisdiction and establish it as residential suburban-20 Falls/Jordan Watershed Overlay B city jurisdiction as part of the Enclave at Little Creek consolidated annexation and UDO changes. The item followed earlier debate regarding community concerns, public goods, and the appropriate regulatory standards for urban expansion in Durham. Council Members Nate Baker and Carl R. Burris voted against the zoning designation change, while the majority approved the motion 4-2.

votes.item_title: Consolidated Annexation - Enclave at Little Creek (Item 23) - Consistency Statement
votes.discussion_detail: This motion proposed adopting a consistency statement as required by North Carolina General Statutes Section 160D-605 in connection with the Enclave at Little Creek annexation and UDO amendments. Following the roll-call votes on the preceding annexation and zoning ordinance motions, the council voted unanimously to adopt the statutory consistency statement.

disagreements.meeting_title: Durham City Council May 4, 2026
disagreements.issue: Enclave at Little Creek Annexation and Rezoning (Item 23)
disagreements.summary: Debate over the 47.85-acre Enclave at Little Creek annexation and rezoning (PDR 5.006) for up to 230 residential units with 20% affordable housing versus environmental and infrastructure concerns in the Jordan Lake watershed.
disagreements.side_a_position: Support annexation and rezoning for the Enclave at Little Creek development.
side_a_arguments: Durham has an acute housing shortage and rising home prices, requiring increased housing density.
The project includes 20% income-restricted affordable housing, exceeding standard city goals.
The proposal aligns with the comprehensive plan's designation for mixed residential development near transit opportunity areas.
If denied, the property could be developed as low-density single-family estates on well and septic without any affordable housing commitments.
disagreements.side_b_position: Oppose annexation and rezoning due to environmental impact, infrastructure strain, and stormwater risks.
side_b_arguments: Significant environmental and ecological concerns regarding impacts on the natural heritage area and Jordan Lake watershed headwaters.
Stormwater runoff and drainage issues affecting downstream neighborhoods during drought and heavy rain events.
Inadequate walkability, lack of sidewalks, and distance from public transit and amenities.
Concerns that the 20% affordable housing is structured as a separate standalone component rather than fully integrated inclusionary housing.
disagreements.resolution: Passed (4-2)

meetings.title: Durham City Council Work Session April 23, 2026
meetings.executive_summary: The Durham City Council held its Work Session on April 23, 2026, presided over by Mayor Williams. The meeting included tributes to retiring Police Chief Patrice Andrews, an update on the regional drought conditions by Water Management Director Don Greeley, public comments regarding local development and sediment controls, and the suspension of rules to vote on vehicle purchases. The council also discussed and settled upcoming agenda items, moving several resolutions to the General Business Agenda (GBA).

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Roll Call & Council Announcements
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The Durham City Council Work Session was called to order at 1:00 PM by Mayor Williams. Roll call established the presence of Mayor Williams, Mayor Pro Tem Caballero, and Council Members Baker, Burris, Cook, and Kopack, with Council Member Rist excused. Council members shared brief opening announcements and approved excused absences for upcoming meetings.
agenda_items.vote_summary: No formal vote (routine absence votes passed by voice vote)

agenda_items.title: Recognition of Retiring Police Chief Patrice Andrews
agenda_items.discussion_summary: City Manager Ryan Smith, Mayor Williams, and council members offered heartfelt tributes honoring retiring Police Chief Patrice Andrews for her 25 years of service in Durham and 30 years in law enforcement. Chief Andrews delivered emotional remarks reflecting on her career, community trust-building, and the evolution of policing in Durham. Incoming interim chief Walter Tate was also briefly introduced.

agenda_items.title: Manager's Priority Items: Drought Status & Technology Leadership
agenda_items.discussion_summary: City Manager Ryan Smith introduced Richard Barbee as the new Director of Technology Solutions and commended interim director Marcia Richardson. Water Management Director Don Greeley provided a status update on the ongoing drought, noting that Durham County entered extreme drought conditions while lake levels are at 84%, and discussed regional utility coordination.

agenda_items.title: Public Comments
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Members of the public, including Trina Hymes representing Grove Park Homeowners Association, addressed the council regarding stormwater runoff and topographical ridge protection concerning development sites near Little Lick Creek. Other scheduled speakers deferred their comments to upcoming public hearings.

agenda_items.title: Purchase of Tandem Axle Dump Trucks (Transource Inc.)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: City council considered and approved a motion to suspend the rules to immediately vote on two equipment purchase items due to pending price increases. Council authorized contracts with Transource Inc. of Kernersville, NC, for purchasing tandem axle dump trucks for the fleet.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Passed, 6-0 (Motion to suspend rules passed; Item 6 passed 6-0; Item 7 passed 6-0)

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda Review: Resolutions & Policy Discussion
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council reviewed pulled consent agenda items, discussing the Children's Wealth Building Resolution (Item 2), Endangered Species Day Resolution (Item 3), and proposed temporary development moratorium on data centers and cryptocurrency mining facilities (Item 4). Council members debated details and agreed to move several policy resolutions to the General Business Agenda (GBA).
agenda_items.vote_summary: No formal vote (items moved to General Business Agenda for later consideration)

agenda_items.title: Accessible Pedestrian Signals & Work Zone Safety Update
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Transportation Director Sean Egan presented construction contracts and updates regarding signalized pedestrian upgrades across 13 locations, incorporating accessible pedestrian signals (APS) and leading pedestrian intervals. Staff also highlighted roadway work zone safety awareness week, urging drivers to exercise caution and slow down in work zones.

agenda_items.title: GoDurham Fiscal Year Annual Report & Transit Operations
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council reviewed the GoDurham annual report, praising system performance metrics compared to peer cities while discussing fleet age, preventative maintenance contractor performance issues, and regional transit funding shortfalls discussed at joint city-county meetings.

agenda_items.title: Water & Sewer Fund Budget Ordinance Amendment & Agenda Settlement
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Don Greeley and budget staff presented a budget ordinance amendment for water and sewer funds, explaining fund balance transfers required due to reduced vacancy savings as positions were successfully filled. Council subsequently settled the final meeting agenda and adjourned the work session at 2:48 PM.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Passed, 6-0 (Motion to settle agenda passed; meeting adjourned)

votes.item_title: Purchase of five tandem axle dump trucks (Transource Inc.) - Item 6
votes.discussion_detail: Following a motion to suspend the rules, the City Council voted to authorize a contract with Transource Incorporated of Kernersville, North Carolina, for the purchase of five tandem axle dump trucks in the total amount of $1,467,751.75. The motion was moved by Mayor Williams, seconded by Council Member Baker, and passed unanimously (6-0).

votes.item_title: Purchase of five tandem axle dump trucks (Transource Inc.) - Item 7
votes.discussion_detail: Immediately following the previous item, the council considered and approved a second contract with Transource Incorporated of Kernersville, North Carolina, for the purchase of an additional five tandem axle dump trucks totaling $1,270,368,000. The motion was moved by Mayor Williams, seconded by Council Member Baker, and passed unanimously (6-0) following the suspension of the rules.

meetings.title: Durham City Council April 20, 2026
meetings.executive_summary: The Durham City Council met on April 20, 2026, holding ceremonial proclamations and an extensive public hearing on the Morgan Farm annexation and utility extension agreement proposed by MI Homes. Following public comment and council debate regarding environmental sensitivities, watershed protection, stormwater management, and infrastructure capacity, a motion to approve the annexation and utility extension agreement failed in a 5-2 vote.

agenda_items.title: Opening, Moment of Silence, Pledge of Allegiance, and Roll Call
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Leonardo Williams called the meeting to order, followed by a moment of silence and the Pledge of Allegiance led by Council Member Carl Rist. Roll call confirmed all council members were present.

agenda_items.title: National Poetry Month Proclamation
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council Member Shanetta Burris read a proclamation declaring April 2026 as National Poetry Month, joined by Durham Poet Laureate Chris Vitiello, who shared remarks and a special poem about Durham.

agenda_items.title: Tuberous Sclerosis Complex Awareness Day Proclamation
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Williams presented a proclamation declaring May 15, 2026 as Tuberous Sclerosis Complex Awareness Day, joined by Ashley Een and family advocating for TSC awareness and research.

agenda_items.title: Carolina Theatre 100th Anniversary Commemoration
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The council commemorated the 100th anniversary of the Carolina Theatre of Durham, joined by representatives Randy McKay and Rebecca Lee, highlighting its history, civil rights milestone, and economic impact.

agenda_items.title: National Tennis Month Proclamation
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council Member Carl Rist presented a proclamation for National Tennis Month, joined by representatives from DOCTA, EnoCTA, and USTA North Carolina, emphasizing tennis accessibility, health benefits, and local youth programs.

agenda_items.title: Council Member Announcements
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council members shared announcements, including updates on the Durham homeowner grant program, Earth Day and climate action plans, and upcoming May Day international workers' day celebrations.

agenda_items.title: Morgan Farm Annexation and Residential Development Proposal (MI Homes)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Public hearing and deliberation on consolidated annexation cases, including Patterson Hall, Morgan Farm Annexation and Utility Extension Agreement (MI Homes), and Highway 751 parcels. Extensive public comment and council discussion focused on environmental protection, watershed impact on Falls Lake/Jordan Lake, traffic congestion, fire and emergency response times, and sewer infrastructure.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Failed, 5-2 (Mayor Williams and Council Member Wrist voting yes; Council Members Cook, Kopac, Baker, Burrus, and others voting no)

votes.item_title: Morgan Farm Annexation and Utility Extension Agreement
votes.notes: Motion failed 5 to 2, defeating the annexation and development proposal.
votes.discussion_detail: The Durham City Council considered a motion at 2:20 a.m. to adopt an ordinance annexing Morgan Farm into the city of Durham and to authorize the city manager to enter into a utility extension agreement with M/I Homes of Raleigh LLC, incorporating captured profers for a conservation subdivision. Council members debated multiple procedural options, including whether to proceed with annexation alone, separate the utility extension agreement for a later time, or proceed with everything as is including the profer commitments. Dissenting members expressed frustration regarding the large translational zoning parcel with numerous unknown factors, arguing that potential benefits were heavily outweighed by future complications and uncertainties. Ultimately, the motion failed on a 5-2 vote, with Mayor Williams and Council Member Carl Rist voting in favor, while Copac, Cook, Baker, Burris, and another council member voted in opposition.

disagreements.issue: Morgan Farm Annexation and Residential Development Proposal (MI Homes)
disagreements.summary: Debate over whether to approve the annexation and utility extension for a 300+ unit residential development (Morgan Farm) on a sensitive forested site within the Jordan/Falls Lake watershed.
disagreements.side_a_position: Support annexation and development
side_a_arguments: The developer made unprecedented commitments including 50% open space conservation, 8% affordable housing at 80% AMI, and $2 million in transportation and intersection improvements.
Denying annexation leaves landowners with little choice but to timber/log the property or develop with wells and septic without city oversight or conservation benefits.
disagreements.side_b_position: Oppose annexation and development
side_b_arguments: The site has high environmental sensitivity (Triassic Basin soils, steep slopes, proximity to Panther/Little Creek, Falls/Jordan Lake protected watershed).
Translational zoning lacks enforceable protections and stormwater commitments at the rezoning stage, and the Planning Commission voted 9-0 against it.
Inadequate local infrastructure including fire/EMS response times, sewer capacity, and severe traffic congestion on local roads.
disagreements.resolution: The motion to approve annexation and utility extension failed 5-2.

meetings.title: Durham City Council Work Session April 9, 2026
meetings.executive_summary: The Durham City Council held its work session on April 9, 2026, presided over by Mayor Pro Tem Javiera Caballero due to the mayor's excused absence. The council discussed manager priority items including the pavement condition index (PCI) study and legislative priorities for the 2026 short session, received proclamations, heard public comments, and held a closed session regarding threatened liability claims. Formal votes were taken to accept the manager's priority items, approve a closed session, approve an excused absence, and settle the agenda.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Roll Call, and National Public Safety Telecommunications Week Proclamation
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Pro Tem Cabayou called the meeting to order, noting an excused absence for Mayor Williams. The clerk called the roll. The council presented a proclamation recognizing National Public Safety Telecommunications Week to representatives of the Durham Emergency Communications Center.

agenda_items.title: Announcements by Council Members
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council members shared announcements, including concerns regarding the recent deportation of a Durham resident family following an ICE detention in Charlotte, updates from the Durham Workers Rights Commission, potential resolutions for Endangered Species Day and Trump asset building accounts (530A accounts), updates on the Durham Housing Authority exiting troubled status, and upcoming events.

agenda_items.title: Manager's Priority Items, Closed Session Motion, and Excused Absences
agenda_items.discussion_summary: City Manager Ferguson presented priority items, noting that agenda item 7 (pavement condition study) and agenda item 25 (legislative priorities) included presentations, while agenda item 20 was referred back to staff. The council voted to accept the manager's priority items and approved a closed session motion.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Passed, 6-0 (Motions for priority items, closed session, and excused absence)

agenda_items.title: Public Comments
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Public comments were heard from speakers including Scott Harmon regarding land development code and neighborhood character, and Amanda Wallace regarding legislative priorities.

agenda_items.title: ST 332C Pavement Condition Study Presentation
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff presented the 2026 Pavement Condition Index (PCI) study, detailing network pavement conditions, maintenance strategies (reclamation, overlays, cape seals), optimization models, and funding scenarios (comparing $25M vs $35M annual budgets). Council members discussed equity weighting, asphalt vs concrete durability, utility cuts, and plans to publish a 3-5 year paving plan.

agenda_items.title: Legislative Priorities for the 2026 Short Session
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The council reviewed legislative priorities for the 2026 short session, discussing potential shifts to even-year municipal elections, tax loopholes for nonprofit affordable housing, housing supply bills, and advocacy priorities across housing, environmental quality, and transportation buckets.

votes.item_title: Manager's Priority Items Acceptance
votes.discussion_detail: The City Council considered the acceptance of the Manager's Priority Items, following discussion of items pulled from the agenda. Public comments were received from speaker Miss Wallace regarding interlocal agreements, housing, and community services. The council proceeded with agenda management and subsequent business as recorded in the work session.

votes.item_title: Closed Session Motion
votes.discussion_detail: A closed session motion was brought forward during the work session following agenda discussions and public input. The motion was approved unanimously with a 6-0 vote. No dissenting votes or specific conditions were recorded in the excerpt leading up to the motion.

votes.item_title: Excused Absence for Council Member Rist
votes.discussion_detail: An excused absence was noted for Council Member Rist during the proceedings. The council conducted discussions regarding municipal fleet policies, electric bus purchases, federal support, and street maintenance models before taking up administrative items. The motion for the excused absence passed with a 6-0 vote.

meetings.title: Durham City Council April 6, 2026
meetings.executive_summary: The Durham City Council convened on April 6, 2026, hearing ceremonial proclamations and extensive public comment regarding infrastructure, traffic, and flooding. The primary agenda item was the Preserve at Trinity (Sunhouse Realty) rezoning and utility extension request near the Eno River watershed. After robust debate on environmental constraints, traffic impacts, and housing affordability, the council approved the utility extension agreement and rezoning ordinance in 4-3 split votes, along with unanimously approving the consistency statement and excusing the mayor from an upcoming work session.

agenda_items.title: Opening, Moment of Silence, Roll Call
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Leonardo Williams called the meeting to order, followed by the Pledge of Allegiance led by Council Member Reese and a roll call establishing a full quorum of council members.

agenda_items.title: Ceremonial Items and Proclamations
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Proclamations were presented recognizing National Community Development Week, Fair Housing Month, Black Maternal Health Week, and Realtors Week, with remarks from city staff and community partner representatives.

agenda_items.title: Council Member Announcements
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council members shared announcements including appreciation for retiring Audit Services Director Dr. Germaine Brewington, opening night of the Durham Bulls baseball season, and an update on the legislative committee's meeting with state lobbyists Checkmate Government Relations regarding local revenue and transit funding.

agenda_items.title: Preserve at Trinity Rezoning & Utility Extension Agreement
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Public hearing and consideration of a rezoning and utility extension agreement for Sunhouse Realty LLC (Preserve at Trinity), involving approximately 40 acres of residential suburban land, environmental protections, conservation easements, and affordable housing proffers. Extensive public comment and council debate focused on traffic impacts at North Roxboro and Infinity Road, Eno River watershed protection, stormwater management, public school funding contributions, and density compatibility.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Passed, 4-3, with dissenting votes from Council Members Baker, Burris, and Cook.

agenda_items.title: Excuse Mayor from Work Session on April 9, 2026
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council considered and approved excusing Mayor Leonardo Williams from the upcoming work session scheduled for Thursday, April 9, 2026.

votes.item_title: Utility Extension Agreement with Sunhouse Realty LLC
votes.discussion_detail: The City Council considered authorizing a utility extension agreement with Sunhouse Realty LLC. Council members debated the developer's scale and offers compared to community concerns regarding traffic and flooding impacts. Discussion touched on local versus state and federal funding burdens and potential contributions to the Durham Public Schools Foundation. The motion passed by a 4-3 vote, with Council Members Baker, Burris, and Cook voting in opposition.

votes.item_title: Ordinance Amending UDO for Preserve at Trinity Rezoning
votes.discussion_detail: The City Council considered an ordinance to amend the unified development ordinance by removing property from residential suburban 20 Eno Watershed Overlay District B and establishing it as planned development residential 6.185 office and institutional with a development plan. Council discussion regarding development pressures, infrastructure impacts, and community feedback preceded the vote. The motion passed 4-3, with Council Members Baker, Burris, and Cook voting no.

votes.item_title: Consistency Statement for Preserve at Trinity Rezoning (NCGS 160D-605)
votes.discussion_detail: The City Council considered adopting the required consistency statement under North Carolina General Statute Section 160D-605 regarding the Preserve at Trinity rezoning. Following the previous zoning and utility extension discussions, the consistency statement was presented for formal adoption. The motion passed unanimously (7-0).

votes.item_title: Excuse Mayor from Work Session on April 9, 2026
votes.discussion_detail: The City Council considered a procedural motion to excuse the mayor from the upcoming work session scheduled for Thursday, April 9, 2026. The mayor noted the need to be absent and requested facilitation of the motion. The motion was moved, seconded, and passed unanimously (7-0).

disagreements.meeting_title: Durham City Council April 6, 2026
disagreements.issue: Preserve at Trinity (Sunhouse Realty) Rezoning & Utility Extension
disagreements.summary: Debate over whether to approve rezoning and utility extension for a multi-family/townhome and office-institutional development near Infinity Road and the Eno River watershed, balancing housing need against environmental, traffic, and flood risks.
disagreements.side_a_position: Approve the rezoning, utility extension, and consistency statement.
side_a_arguments: The project is consistent with the comprehensive plan and place type map for transit opportunity areas.
Provides alternative housing types and increased affordability (8% AMI units, improved from 5%) by a local small business developer.

Includes significant environmental proffers (conservation easement for floodplain and stream, 100% native trees in OID, stormwater peak flow mitigation) and increased school donations ($1,000 per student).
disagreements.side_b_position: Deny the rezoning and utility extension project.
side_b_arguments: Severe concerns regarding increased traffic congestion on North Roxboro and Infinity Road, compounded by unfunded state intersection improvements (STIP U-5516).
Environmental and watershed risks including proximity to the Eno River critical area, steep slopes, historical flooding in the area, and potential runoff impacts.
Insufficient affordable housing contribution relative to community need and potential displacement pressures.
disagreements.resolution: Passed 4-3 on the utility extension agreement and UDO amendment ordinance; passed unanimously on the consistency statement.

meetings.title: Durham City Council Work Session March 19, 2026
meetings.executive_summary: The Durham City Council held a work session on March 19, 2026. The council discussed routine announcements, proclamations (declaring Cleaning Week), board and committee appointments, public comments regarding fire station vehicle break-ins and property conditions, a major review of options for the 505 West Chapel Hill Street site (including affordable housing and historic preservation of the Milton Small Building), and administrative updates to council agenda formatting. No formal roll-call votes or motions were recorded in this work session transcript.

agenda_items.title: Council Member Announcements
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council members shared opening announcements, including Council Member Matt Kopac mentioning the Environmental Affairs Board letter on Duke Energy's carbon plan, Council Member Carl Rist highlighting March Madness and upcoming parks bond public meetings, and the Mayor Pro Tem discussing the reporting on Cesar Chavez and community survivors.

agenda_items.title: Proclamation for Cleaning Week (General Services Custodial Team)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Leonardo Williams and the city council recognized the General Services Department custodial team and celebrated upcoming International Cleaning Week (cleaning week in Durham), highlighting the city's commitment to in-house cleaning staff with competitive wages and benefits rather than third-party outsourcing.

agenda_items.title: Priority Items, City Attorney Introduction, and Board & Committee Reports
agenda_items.discussion_summary: City Manager reported no priority items for the City Manager's Office. City Attorney reported no priority items and introduced a new paralegal, Maryann Frati, focusing on affordable housing and real estate. City Clerk reported board and committee appointments (Daniel W. Cole, Lena G. Tonkan, Nicholas Monton, Priesty Willis) and noted lack of consensus for the Human Relations Commission appointment.

agenda_items.title: Public Comment: Fire Station Vehicle Break-ins (Local 668)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Meredith Carter spoke on behalf of Local 668 (Professional Firefighters of Durham) regarding frequent personal vehicle break-ins at fire stations across the city (stations 1, 3, 4, 5, 9, 12, and 16). She requested secure fencing or mobile security at every station and city support for vehicle repairs.

agenda_items.title: Public Comment: Council Punctuality, St. Joseph Historical Foundation, and Blighted Properties
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Victoria Peterson expressed concern about council members and the mayor arriving late to work sessions, requested an itemized budget report regarding St. Joseph Historical Foundation and the $10M fund, and reported run-down properties on Ridgeway Avenue, Austin Avenue, and Fayetteville Street.

agenda_items.title: Public Comment: Land Development Code (LDC), Infill Standards, and Zoning Inequities
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Scott Harmon, architect and developer with Center Studio, spoke about historical zoning patterns, neighborhood character, minimum lot sizes, and how current infill standards in the Land Development Code (LDC) perpetuate systemic inequities in housing and land use.

agenda_items.title: 505 West Chapel Hill Street Site Redevelopment & Milton Small Building Preservation
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council and staff discussed the 505 West Chapel Hill Street site redevelopment options, incorporating affordable housing, preserving the Milton Small Building with Preservation North Carolina, parking strategies, and coordination with financing partners. Extensive discussion took place on infill, tax credits, and future site activation.

agenda_items.title: City Council Agenda Format Updates
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff presented proposed updates to city council agenda formats, including the creation of a 'No Action Matters' informational section at the end of regular business meetings for disposed/referred items, and updating the timing and placement of citizens matters in work session agendas.

meetings.title: Durham City Council March 16, 2026 (Full Audio)
meetings.executive_summary: The Durham City Council held its regular meeting on March 16, 2026, featuring several proclamations, public hearings on the upcoming FY 2027 budget and CIP, and votes on capital financing and zoning changes. The council debated and approved amendments to the Fayetteville Street Corridor Neighborhood Stabilization Partnership and grant agreement with Hataway Promise Community Development Corporation (removing St. Joseph's Historic Foundation as fiscal agent) in a 5-2 split vote. Additionally, the council unanimously approved a $136 million limited obligation bond resolution for capital projects, solid waste, and DPAC HVAC reimbursements, as well as a zoning map change for 1612 and 1562 Carpenter Fletcher Road.

agenda_items.title: Opening, Pledge of Allegiance & Roll Call
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor pro tem opened the meeting, followed by a moment of silent meditation, the Pledge of Allegiance, and roll call confirming council members present.

agenda_items.title: Proclamations & Special Presentations
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council members read and presented proclamations for Bleeding Disorders Awareness Month, Durham Crop Hunger Walk, and International Women's History Month.

agenda_items.title: Council Member Announcements
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council members shared community updates, recognized local sports achievements (Southern High School 7A state championship), and highlighted upcoming events and creek cleanups.

agenda_items.title: Fayetteville Street Corridor Stabilization & Hataway Promise CDC Grant Agreement Amendments
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Extensive public comments and council debate regarding the first amendment to the ARPA/Revenue Recovery Subrecipient Grant Agreement and Fayetteville Street Corridor Neighborhood Stabilization Partnership with Hataway Promise CDC and St. Joseph's Historic Foundation. Discussion focused on fiscal oversight, transparency, community engagement, and progress tracking.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Passed (5-2 on Item 12.1; unanimous on subsequent modifications and partnership amendments).

agenda_items.title: Limited Obligation Bonds Series 2026AB Installment Financing Contract
agenda_items.discussion_summary: City debt administrator presented the proposed limited obligation bond series 2026AB (not to exceed $136 million) to fund general capital projects, solid waste, and DPAC HVAC project costs. Public hearing was held with no speakers signed up.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Passed unanimously (Unanimous vote on installment financing contract resolution and legal document execution).

agenda_items.title: Zoning Map Change for 1612 and 1562 Carpenter Fletcher Road
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Planning staff and applicant presented a zoning map change request for 1612 and 1562 Carpenter Fletcher Road from Commercial General with textual development plan and office/institutional to Commercial General with textual development plan to expand permitted uses and commit to native landscaping species.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Passed unanimously (Unanimous vote on zoning map ordinance and consistency statement).

agenda_items.title: FY 2027 Budget & Capital Improvement Plan Public Hearing
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Budget and Management Services director presented the public hearing to receive comments on the development of the FY 2027 budget and FY 2027-2032 Capital Improvement Plan (CIP).

votes.item_title: First Amendment to ARPA/Revenue Recovery Subrecipient Grant Agreement with Hataway Promise Community Development Corporation
votes.notes: Removes St. Joseph's Historic Foundation as fiscal agent and updates funding source up to $6,755,000.
votes.discussion_detail: This vote concerned the first amendment to the ARPA/Revenue Recovery Subrecipient Grant Agreement with Hataway Promise Community Development Corporation, involving a total amount not to exceed $6,755,000 to remove St. Joseph's Historic Foundation Inc. as fiscal agent and change the funding source. Council members debated major work products, reporting intervals, and community engagement, with Council Member Baker requesting reports at 6- to 12-month intervals until funds are fully expended. The motion passed 5-2, with Council Members Burris and Cook voting in opposition.

votes.item_title: Subsequent Modifications Authorization for Hataway Promise CDC Grant Agreement
votes.notes: Authorizes city manager to negotiate and make subsequent modifications up to $6,755,000.
votes.discussion_detail: This routine motion authorized the city manager to negotiate and make subsequent modifications to the amended grant agreement with Hataway Promise Community Development Corporation, provided that total grant funds do not exceed $6,755,000. The motion passed unanimously without recorded debate or opposition.

votes.item_title: Fayetteville Street Corridor Neighborhood Stabilization Partnership Agreement Amendment
votes.notes: First amendment involving Hataway Promise CDC, City of Durham, and Preserving Home Inc. to remove St. Joseph Historic Foundation as fiscal agent.
votes.discussion_detail: This vote authorized the first amendment to the agreement between Hataway Promise Community Development Corporation, the City of Durham, and Preserving Home Inc. (formerly Rebuilding Together of the Triangle Inc.) for the Fayetteville Street corridor neighborhood stabilization partnership implementation. The amendment removed St. Joseph Historic Foundation Inc. as fiscal agent. The motion passed unanimously.

votes.item_title: Limited Obligation Bonds Series 2026AB Installment Financing Contract
votes.notes: Approving installment financing contract not to exceed $136 million for general capital, solid waste, and DPAC HVAC project costs.
votes.discussion_detail: This vote adopted a resolution approving an installment financing contract not to exceed $136 million along with an accompanying deed of trust, and provided for a public hearing concerning the contract to finance general capital, solid waste, and DPAC (Durham Arts) needs as presented by debt administrator John Reese. The motion passed unanimously.

votes.item_title: Execution of Legal Documents for 2026AB Limited Obligation Bonds
votes.notes: Authorizing city manager/designate to execute associated legal documents.
votes.discussion_detail: Following the adoption of the financing contract, this vote authorized the city manager or his designate to execute other associated legal documents and make pre-execution changes consistent with the intent of the agenda item memo and existing document versions. The motion passed unanimously.

votes.item_title: Zoning Map Change for 1612 and 1562 Carpenter Fletcher Road
votes.notes: Expanding permitted uses under Commercial General with textual development plan, including commitment to native species landscaping.
votes.discussion_detail: The council considered a zoning map change for 1612 and 1562 Carpenter Fletcher Road, amending the unified development ordinance to transition property out of commercial general with a textual development plan in office and institutional and establishing the same as commercial general with the textual development plan. meetings.title: Durham City Council Work Session March 5, 2026
meetings.executive_summary: The Durham City Council held its work session on March 5, 2026, discussing critical infrastructure and community development items, including a wastewater collection system capacity overview highlighting capacity constraints in the Goose Creek basin and upcoming infrastructure projects, as well as an implementation update on the Fayetteville Street Corridor Neighborhood Stabilization Partnership involving Hayti Promise CDC. The council also heard extensive public comments on unpaved streets, traffic fatalities, park encampments, and gun violence, settled the meeting agenda, and voted to enter a closed session for attorney-client consultation and property damage claims.

agenda_items.title: Roll Call, Announcements, and Opening Remarks
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Williams called the work session to order, followed by a roll call and brief council announcements, including updates on joint city-county planning, environmental boards, and birthday wishes for Councilmember Kopac. Several councilmembers also raised community concerns regarding recent gun violence in Durham and conditions in correctional facilities.

agenda_items.title: Manager and Attorney Priorities & Closed Session Motion
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The City Manager reviewed priority items, noting the withdrawal of one speaker under citizen matters. The City Attorney requested a closed session regarding pending federal litigation (Timothy Evans v. City of Durham et al.) and a property damage claim by Capital Associates, which was approved by unanimous voice vote.

agenda_items.title: DPAC Oversight Committee Mayoral Appointment
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The City Clerk presented the mayoral appointment for the Durham Performing Arts Center (DPAC) Oversight Committee, recommending Scott F. Selig.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda Reading and Item Pulls
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The Mayor read the consent agenda items, and councilmembers discussed and pulled specific items for separate discussion and public comment (including items 10, 12, 13, and 14).

agenda_items.title: Citizen Matters / Public Comment
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Residents spoke during citizen matters on various topics, including unpaved street and water infrastructure needs on Ottmar Drive, traffic safety and district attorney accountability regarding hit-and-run fatalities, park encampments at Oakwood Park, and gun violence prevention.

agenda_items.title: Wastewater Collection System Capacity Overview Presentation
agenda_items.discussion_summary: City staff delivered a comprehensive presentation on wastewater collection system capacity, focusing on the unexpected 100% capacity finding in the Goose Creek basin, ongoing outfall improvement projects, hydraulic modeling, and the issuance of Letters to Industry (LTIs) restricting development. Councilmembers questioned staff extensively regarding notice transparency and project timelines.

agenda_items.title: Fayetteville Street Corridor Project Implementation Update
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff and representatives presented an update on the Fayetteville Street Corridor Neighborhood Stabilization Partnership Implementation, detailing the deployment of ARPA funds, historic preservation partnerships (Preservation Durham, Preserving Home Inc.), youth workforce training, and governance structures of the Hayti Promise CDC. Public speakers and councilmembers debated oversight, financial transparency, and community engagement.

agenda_items.title: Settle Agenda for Forthcoming Meeting
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The City Manager reviewed the items to be placed on the agenda for the forthcoming formal council meeting, and the council voted to settle the agenda.

votes.item_title: Closed Session (Timothy Evans v. City of Durham & Capital Associates property damage claim)
votes.discussion_detail: The City Attorney proposed a motion to resume into closed session post-agenda to discuss two legal matters: a federal district case in the Middle District (case 26-CV-181) involving Timothy Evans v. City of Durham, Irwin Baker, and James Edward Melvin II, as well as a property damage claim presented by Capital Associates and CPD Durham Center Investors. The motion was properly moved, seconded, and passed unanimously by voice vote with no opposition. Following the vote, the Clerk delivered board and committee reports, including the mayoral appointment of Scott F. Selig to the Durham Performing Arts Center Oversight Committee, followed by the reading of the consent agenda.

disagreements.meeting_title: Durham City Council Work Session March 5, 2026
disagreements.issue: Communication and notification transparency regarding wastewater capacity Letters to Industry in the Goose Creek basin
disagreements.summary: Councilmembers debated whether issuing letters to industry restricting development due to sewer capacity constraints without direct mailings to affected property owners was sufficient.
disagreements.side_a_position: Standard administrative practice via industry associations is sufficient.
side_a_arguments: LTIs were distributed through standard channels like the Home Builders Association and voluntary sign-up lists, consistent with past practice.
disagreements.side_b_position: Direct mailings or expanded property records outreach should be used to notify affected property owners.
side_b_arguments: Property owners were caught by surprise with halted development rights without direct notice or due process.
disagreements.resolution: Staff agreed to evaluate expanding notification methods and budgetary impacts for property-specific letters to industry in the future.

disagreements.meeting_title: Durham City Council Work Session March 5, 2026
disagreements.issue: Accountability, structure, and oversight of ARPA funding and community development for the Fayetteville Street Corridor (Hayti Promise CDC)
disagreements.summary: Councilmembers and community members debated the effectiveness, administrative hurdles, and oversight surrounding the Hayti Promise CDC and ARPA investments.
disagreements.side_a_position: Supportive of the bold ARPA investment and volunteer board efforts.
side_a_arguments: The initial ARPA allocation was a bold, necessary community-led risk and down payment addressing historical underinvestment in the corridor.
disagreements.side_b_position: Expressed caution and concern over administrative overhead, financial controls, and accountability.
side_b_arguments: High consultant expenditures, lack of established organizational capacity, and questions over financial transparency raised red flags.
disagreements.resolution: Discussion concluded with consensus on maintaining oversight, auditing future expenditures, and supporting ongoing corridor revitalization efforts while demanding accountability.

meetings.title: Durham City Council March 2, 2026
meetings.executive_summary: The Durham City Council met on March 2, 2026, led by Mayor Leonardo Williams. The council recognized National Girl Scout Day, honored three GoDurham bus operators with Million Miler Club awards, and heard extensive public comments regarding gun violence, youth safety, and community investments. The council unanimously adopted the consent agenda (7-0) and later accepted the Fourth Quarter Crime Report (Item 12) also by a 7-0 vote. Council members also discussed upcoming difficult budget deliberations, including priorities such as fare-free buses and emergency home repairs.

agenda_items.title: Opening Roll Call, Pledge of Allegiance, and Girl Scouts & GoDurham Proclamations
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The meeting opened with a roll call, a moment of silence, and the Pledge of Allegiance. Council presented ceremonial proclamations recognizing National Girl Scout Day and honoring three GoDurham bus operators inducted into the Million Miler Club for driving 1 million safe miles.

agenda_items.title: City Council Member Announcements & Regional Updates
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council members shared announcements regarding local business incubator openings, labor union events, community health fairs, condolences for fallen state trooper Steven Perry, concerns over ongoing conflicts in the Middle East, and upcoming budget retreat priorities and public hearings.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda (Items 1-11, 13-14)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The City Manager and Attorney provided brief administrative updates. Council reviewed and adopted the consent agenda, which included board appointments, financial reports, grant budget ordinances, contract awards, and interlocal agreements.

agenda_items.title: Public Comments on Community Safety and Crime
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Numerous community members, youth advocates, and student leaders spoke during public comment regarding community safety, youth violence, policing history, mental health support, and the need for greater investment in youth employment and community violence intervention initiatives.

agenda_items.title: 2025 Fourth Quarter Crime Report (Item 12)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Following public comments on crime and safety, the council took up Item 12, the 2025 Fourth Quarter Crime Report, which had been pulled from the consent agenda for consideration and discussion.

votes.item_title: Consent Agenda (excluding pulled items)
votes.discussion_detail: The council considered the adoption of the consent agenda (excluding pulled item number 12), which covered various committee appointments, financial and annual reports, grants, contracts, structural repairs, bonds, and interlocal agreements. Following the presentation of the agenda items by the mayor, a motion was properly made and seconded to adopt the consent agenda. The motion passed unanimously with a 7-0 vote.

votes.item_title: 2025 Fourth Quarter Crime Report (Item 12)
votes.discussion_detail: The council considered item 12, the 2025 Fourth Quarter Crime Report, following public comments addressing community safety, youth violence, and municipal budget priorities. Public speakers and council members discussed strategies around youth violence reduction, asset mapping, and potential collaborations with a violence reduction center to address root causes of crime. Public speaker Donald Hughes raised concerns regarding the city's budget allocations, emphasizing the need for investments in youth employment, community compassion, and systemic support rather than punitive approaches. Mayor Williams and council members responded by emphasizing engagement around community safety and focusing support on youth. Following discussion and public input, a motion to accept the 2025 Fourth Quarter Crime Report was properly made and seconded, passing unanimously with a 7-0 vote.

meetings.title: Durham City Council Budget Retreat: Day 2 - Friday, February 27, 2026 Part 1
meetings.executive_summary: Durham City Council held Day 2 of their budget retreat on Friday, February 27, 2026. City Manager Bo Ferguson briefed the council on severe fiscal constraints, warning that rising expenditures and constrained revenues will make achieving a balanced budget challenging and require difficult choices. Transportation Director Sean Egan also presented the transit and parking fund update, highlighting growing financial deficits and confirming that previous fund surplus projections have worsened.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order and Roll Call
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Williams called the Durham City Council Budget Retreat (Day 2, Part 1) to order at 9:02 AM. Madam Clerk called the roll, establishing a quorum with Mayor Williams, Mayor Pro Tem Javiera Caballero, and Council Members Baker, Burus, Cook, Copac, and Rest present.

agenda_items.title: Day 2 Budget Retreat Overview and Opening Remarks
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Budget and Management Services Director Christina Rearden outlined the full agenda for Day 2 of the budget retreat, highlighting morning sessions covering the City Manager's remarks, transit and parking fund updates, and Capital Improvement Program (CIP) discussions, followed by afternoon working sessions on city council budget requests, strategic plan priorities, and budget guidelines.

agenda_items.title: City Manager's Budget Outlook and Opening Remarks
agenda_items.discussion_summary: City Manager Bo Ferguson delivered candid opening remarks expressing serious stress regarding the FY2026/2027 revenue and expenditure outlook, noting that revenue projections are underperforming while expenditure pressures are mounting. He emphasized that difficult choices and potential cuts will be necessary to achieve a balanced budget, and called on council members to practice rigorous and tactful honesty when prioritizing initiatives.

agenda_items.title: Transit Fund Financial Status and Revenue Update
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Transportation Director Sean Egan and City Manager Bo Ferguson presented a critical financial update on the Transit Fund, recalling warnings from the previous year's budget retreat regarding fund balance depletion. They reported that the transit fund financial position has worsened due to underperforming revenues, presenting significant challenges for maintaining transit commitments and fare-free service.
