meetings.title: Durham City Council Budget Retreat: Day 2 - Friday, February 27, 2026 - Part 3
meetings.executive_summary: The Durham City Council held Day 2 of their 2026 Budget Retreat (Part 3), discussing the 10-year Capital Improvement Program (CIP) model, debt capacity limits, and general fund revenue and expenditure balancing. Council members debated project prioritization frameworks, mayoral budget requests (such as funding for the 2029 World University Games and local economic activation), and options for closing the general fund budget gap without excessive property tax increases. The session served as a strategic working retreat to provide guidance to the city manager for upcoming budget recommendations, with no formal roll-call votes or binding legislative actions taken.

agenda_items.title: Capital Improvement Program (CIP) 10-Year Plan & Process Overview
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff presented an overview of the 10-year Capital Improvement Program (CIP) budget process, highlighting the receipt of 70 general capital project requests totaling over $200 million for FY27. Council members discussed the need for long-term predictability, realism regarding construction cost overruns, and enhanced transparency for residents.

agenda_items.title: Finance Department & Debt Model Overview
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Finance Director Tim Flora reviewed the city's debt model, fund cash flows, debt portfolio exceeding $1 billion ($614M utilities, $394M governmental), and key financial ratios (debt service as % of operating expense, debt per capita, and adherence to AAA credit rating targets).

agenda_items.title: Strategic Priority Buckets & Prioritization Framework Structure
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council members debated the strategic priority buckets and prioritization framework structure, specifically addressing how to handle multiple overlapping goals, whether to split complex environmental/housing buckets, and how council-submitted initiatives interact with departmental requests.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Consensus reached via sticky-note voting and inclusion of additional categories without formal roll call tally.

agenda_items.title: General Fund Budget Gap Balancing & Revenue Options
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Finance staff presented preliminary general fund budget balancing options, including tax rate allocations (property tax, debt service, solid waste, dedicated housing, transit) and trade-offs between tax increases, employee pay-for-performance/step plans, and minimum livable wage adjustments.

disagreements.meeting_title: Durham City Council Budget Retreat: Day 2 - Friday, February 27, 2026 - Part 3
disagreements.issue: Strategic Priority Buckets & Prioritization Framework Structure
disagreements.summary: Debate over whether to consolidate or separate categories in the strategic priority framework and how council member priorities fit alongside departmental submissions.
disagreements.side_a_position: Favorable to more granular category separation and tracking council priorities.
side_a_arguments: Argued for separating out specific categories (like resilience/environmental policies or distinct priority areas) and ensuring council member-specific initiatives and earmarks are clearly evaluated alongside departmental requests.
disagreements.side_b_position: Favorable to streamlined, focused priority buckets.
side_b_arguments: Emphasized that strategy is about choice, too many priorities dilute focus, and the ranking tool / sticky-note exercise provides clear directional signals to staff without needing overly fragmented goal categories.
disagreements.resolution: Council agreed to proceed with the structured priority ranking exercise while allowing individual council members to add specific items/priorities and use stickers for weighted preference signaling.

disagreements.meeting_title: Durham City Council Budget Retreat: Day 2 - Friday, February 27, 2026 - Part 3
disagreements.issue: General Fund Budget Gap Balancing: Tax Increases vs. Compensation and Wage Adjustments
disagreements.summary: Discussion and debate over how to close the projected general fund budget gap and whether to raise property taxes or modify step plans, pay-for-performance, and part-time DMLW implementation.
disagreements.side_a_position: Reluctant to raise taxes; open to exploring targeted expenditure adjustments.
side_a_arguments: Strongly opposed raising property taxes due to resident tax fatigue and economic pressures, suggesting exploring reductions in pay-for-performance step percentages (e.g., from 5% down to 4%) or staging part-time DMLW implementations.
disagreements.side_b_position: Cautious about rolling back worker commitments while recognizing fiscal constraints.
side_b_arguments: Highlighted the importance of honoring commitments to city workers, maintaining living wage standards, and preserving employee benefits while acknowledging difficult fiscal trade-offs.
disagreements.resolution: No formal vote taken; staff were directed to provide detailed scenarios and impact analyses on various revenue and expenditure balancing options for upcoming budget hearings.

agenda_items.title: Go Durham Access Paratransit Financial Model & Cost Pressures

disagreements.meeting_title: Durham City Council Work Session Feb 19, 2026
disagreements.issue: Western Intake Partnership (WIP) withdrawal by partner utilities and long-term infrastructure planning/costs
disagreements.summary: Discussion regarding the Western Intake Partnership after partner utilities opted out of upfront participation, focusing on regionalism, capital costs, water quality, and rate impacts.
disagreements.side_a_position: Expressed concern over the loss of regional partnership while acknowledging the necessity of moving forward with the project for Durham's water security.
side_a_arguments: Council members and city staff noted that the withdrawal of partner utilities is a loss for regionalism and changes cost recovery timelines down the road, making finished water costs primarily Durham's responsibility.
disagreements.side_b_position: Maintained that despite partner withdrawal, the project remains the best decision for Durham's long-term water needs and operational efficiency.
side_b_arguments: City staff and management emphasized that upfront capital costs for Durham remain unchanged, and operational savings (such as treating water closer to Durham and utilizing raw water integration) will help offset future cost differences.
disagreements.resolution: Durham City Council received updates and discussed the situation, noting that while partner utilities withdrew from participating upfront, Durham would proceed as the first mover and maintain the raw water intake capacity for future regional use, with operational savings offsetting future costs.

meetings.executive_summary: The Durham City Council convened on February 16, 2026, to discuss community announcements, violent crime rates, homelessness strategies, and budget retreat updates, followed by a public hearing and extensive deliberations on the Lee Village Center mixed-use rezoning and annexation request. After negotiating numerous proffers regarding affordable housing percentages, park land dedication and financial contributions, tree coverage, and pedestrian connectivity, the council unanimously approved the utility extension agreement, zoning ordinance amendments, and consistency statement for the project.

agenda_items.title: Opening, Roll Call, and Council Announcements
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The meeting opened with a moment of silence, the Pledge of Allegiance, and the roll call. Council members delivered announcements regarding upcoming community events, local meetings, and municipal updates.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda Approval
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The City Council reviewed and approved the consent agenda, which included routine items, municipal contracts, and project authorizations, with specific items pulled for separate discussion.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing: FY 2026-2027 Annual Action Plan
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff presented the proposed fiscal year 2026-2027 annual action plan for affordable housing and community development needs in Durham neighborhoods, followed by public comments.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing & Consideration: Lee Village Center Annexation & Rezoning
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Public hearing and deliberation on a request for utility extension agreement, voluntary annexation, and initial zoning map change for Lee Village Center across multiple parcels.

votes.item_title: Utility Extension Agreement with NGR Investment LLC (Lee Village Center)
votes.notes: Passed unanimously after extensive negotiations on proffers.
votes.discussion_detail: The City Council considered a motion to authorize the city manager to enter into a utility extension agreement with NGR Investment LLC for the Lee Village Center project. Discussion leading up to the vote involved commitments regarding pedestrian-oriented design for non-residential buildings, minimum 12-foot sidewalks, commercial use design standards, and a one-time donation of $100,000 to the Durham Parks Foundation alongside at least 2 acres of land dedicated to parks and rec. Additional provisions included a minimum of 10% duplex units, 9,500 square feet of commercial space, AMI terms for townhouse duplexes set at a 30-year tenure, environmentally sensitive open space, and an extra acre of tree coverage. meetings.title: Durham City Council Budget Retreat - Friday, February 13, 2026
meetings.executive_summary: The Durham City Council held its budget retreat and public hearings for the fiscal year 2026-27 budget and capital improvement plan, reviewing financial projections, maintaining a proposed property tax rate of 43.71 cents, and hearing extensive public comment regarding affordable housing, eviction diversion funding, immigration legal services, community safety, violence reduction, and environmental justice cleanup.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order & Opening Remarks
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor and council members opened the budget retreat meeting with roll call and opening remarks welcoming attendees to the Durham County facility. City manager and budget staff outlined the scope of the two-day budget retreats focused on aligning the budget with the strategic plan refresh.

agenda_items.title: City Manager Budget Retreat Kickoff & Strategic Priorities
agenda_items.discussion_summary: City manager delivered the budget retreat opening address, setting the tone for the upcoming budget process. The address emphasized balancing ongoing commitments with new priorities using a chess and jigsaw metaphor for sequencing municipal investments.

agenda_items.title: Financial Update & Budget Outlook
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Budget and management services presented financial projections and a fiscal outlook for the city. Staff reviewed property tax trends, the recent revaluation impacts from the prior year, and expected revenues for the upcoming fiscal year.

agenda_items.title: Staff Compensation & Livable Wage Update
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Human resources staff presented compensation updates, focusing on staff retention, salary structures, and the impact of the Durham Minimum Livable Wage policy on the city's personnel budget.

agenda_items.title: Transit Operations & Capital Improvements Update
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff presented updates on transit operations, including funding requirements for the zero-fare transit program, capital projects, and maintaining transit infrastructure under growing cost pressures.

agenda_items.title: Resident Satisfaction Survey Results
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff presented the results of the resident satisfaction survey, providing statistically valid feedback from across Durham on municipal service delivery, community priorities, and quality of life indicators.

agenda_items.title: Community Conversations & Housing Stability Discussion
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff and council discussed community conversation findings regarding housing and neighborhood stability, rental pressures, displacement risks, and affordable housing needs across Durham.

votes.item_title: FY 2026-27 Budget Public Hearings & Strategic Plan Discussion
votes.discussion_detail: The meeting opened with a roll call by city leadership, confirming the presence of Council members Nate Baker, Shanetta Burr, Chelsea Cook, Matt Kovac, and Crist, alongside the city manager, attorney, and clerk. Director Christina Rearen of the budget and management services department welcomed council members to the first of two budget retreats held on Friday the 13th, providing housekeeping details regarding facilities. Director Rearen outlined that the primary focus of the session was a strategic plan refresh designed to directly drive the upcoming fiscal year budget over the two-day retreat.

disagreements.issue: Eviction Diversion and Legal Aid Funding vs Landlord Impacts
disagreements.summary: Debate between housing advocates supporting eviction diversion/legal aid funding and landlords/housing providers concerned about financial impacts and housing supply reductions.
disagreements.side_a_position: Pro-Funding / Tenant Protection
side_a_arguments: Legal aid and eviction diversion programs are essential anti-displacement tools that prevent homelessness, protect vulnerable tenants, and hold landlords accountable.
disagreements.side_b_position: Critical of Legal Aid Funding / Landlord Perspective
side_b_arguments: Extensive legal aid involvement and delay tactics increase financial hardship for housing providers/landlords, reduce affordable housing supply, and can lead to property sales rather than continued affordable rentals.
side_b_members: David Mafully and other housing providers
disagreements.resolution: Public comments and council discussions addressed the tension between funding legal aid for eviction diversion versus landlord financial impacts and housing supply, with the manager's proposed budget maintaining the prior year's commitment.

meetings.title: Durham City Council Work Session Feb 5, 2026 (full meeting)
meetings.executive_summary: The Durham City Council held its work session on February 5, 2026, chaired by Mayor Pro Tem Javiera Caballero in the absence of Mayor Williams. The council discussed and received annual reports from various boards and commissions, reviewed priority items including a capital improvement contract for radio tower site additions and relocation with Motorola Solutions, and engaged in an in-depth discussion with planning staff regarding riparian buffer protection standards and No Practical Alternatives (NPA) authorizations. The council also approved excused absences for upcoming meetings and officially settled the meeting agenda.

agenda_items.title: Roll Call & Council Member Announcements
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Opening roll call was held noting Mayor Williams excused. Council members shared announcements regarding city workers during winter weather, board and commission annual reports, Black History Month events, white flag shelter extensions, and transit equity day.

agenda_items.title: City Manager's Priority Items & Introductions
agenda_items.discussion_summary: City Manager highlighted priority agenda item 6 regarding radio tower site additions due to expiring bids and introduced new Human Resources Director Aaron Miley while recognizing outgoing acting HR director Montique.

agenda_items.title: Excused Absences for Council Members Burris and Copek
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council members requested and were granted excused absences for the upcoming February 19, 2026 work session.

agenda_items.title: Public Comments & Citizen Matters
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Public comments were delivered regarding public tennis court maintenance and USA tennis programming opportunities in Durham, as well as water quality advocacy by Sound Rivers.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda Pulls & Radio Tower Contract Authorization (Project CB032)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council reviewed pulled consent items, suspended rules for agenda item 6, authorized a contract with Motorola Solutions, Inc. for Project CB032 not to exceed $7,716,771.30, and adopted budget ordinance No. 1655 amending the FY 2025-2026 budget.

agenda_items.title: Riparian Buffer Protection Standards Presentation
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Planning and development staff presented an overview of riparian buffer protection standards, No Practical Alternatives Authorizations (NPA), mitigation options, and variance procedures, followed by extensive council Q&A and public comments.

agenda_items.title: Agenda Settlement and Adjournment
agenda_items.discussion_summary: City Manager reviewed finalized consent items, pulled items, and upcoming public hearings (including adding the Creekside zoning case for Feb 19 as item 29), and council voted to settle the agenda before adjourning.

votes.item_title: Excused absence for Council Member Burrus on February 19, 2026
votes.discussion_detail: Council Member Shanetta Burris requested an excused absence for the upcoming council meeting on February 19, 2026. A motion was offered by Council Member Matt Kopac and seconded by Council Member Carl Rist, and the request was approved unanimously by the council.

votes.item_title: Excused absence for Council Member Copek on February 19, 2026
votes.discussion_detail: Following the earlier excused absence approval, Council Member Matt Kopac requested an excused absence for the same date of February 19, 2026. A motion was made by Council Member Cook and seconded by Council Member Baker, and the request carried unanimously.

votes.item_title: Suspend the rules for Agenda Item 6 (Radio tower site additions and relocation with Motorola Solutions, Inc.)
votes.discussion_detail: To accommodate business regarding Agenda Item 6 concerning radio tower site additions and relocation with Motorola Solutions, Inc., a motion to suspend the rules and vote was introduced. The motion was moved by Council Member Baker and seconded by Council Member Carl Rist, and successfully passed with unanimous support.

votes.item_title: Authorize contract with Motorola Solutions, Inc. for Project CB032 not to exceed $7,716,71.30
votes.discussion_detail: The council considered authorizing the city manager to negotiate and execute a contract with Motorola Solutions, Inc. to complete capital improvement project CB032 in an amount not to exceed $7,716,71.30. The motion was moved by Council Member Baker and seconded by Council Member Cook, passing unanimously without any recorded opposition.

votes.item_title: Adopt budget ordinance amending FY 2025-2026 budget (Ordinance No. 1655) for radio tower project CB032
votes.discussion_detail: As a companion measure to the Motorola Solutions contract for capital improvement project CB032, a motion was presented to adopt a budget ordinance amending the FY 2025-2026 city budget, designated as Ordinance Number 1655, for the purpose of adding additional funding to the project. The motion was moved by Council Member Baker and seconded by Council Member Carl Rist, and passed unanimously.

votes.item_title: Settle the meeting agenda
votes.discussion_detail: Following a rich discussion covering developer proffer details, stringent stream regulations, and the impacts on regular homeowners versus large developers, the City Manager presented the proposed meeting agenda. The agenda included consent items 1 through 5 and 7 through 24, GBA public hearings items 26 and 27, and the addition of item 29 (the creekside item). Council Member Carl Rist moved to settle the agenda, seconded by Council Member Cook, and the motion carried unanimously before the meeting adjourned at 3:10 p.m.

meetings.title: Durham City Council Meeting February 2, 2026 (Virtual)
meetings.executive_summary: The Durham City Council held a virtual meeting on February 2, 2026, due to winter weather conditions. The council unanimously voted to refer a controversial contract with Peregrine Technologies for a police operations management platform back to staff. They also approved the manager's priority items, several consent agenda items, appointments to the Durham Performing Arts Center oversight committee, and adopted a substitute motion for the Curly Gardens annexation/utility extension allowing city water service to be extended to the property without full annexation.

agenda_items.title: Opening, Roll Call & Virtual Meeting Housekeeping
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Williams called the virtual meeting to order at 7:00 PM, followed by a moment of silence and the Pledge of Allegiance. City Clerk conducted the roll call, and the Mayor outlined housekeeping rules for the virtual Zoom webinar format.

agenda_items.title: Council Member Announcements & Recognitions
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council members shared announcements, recognizing Black History Month, local frontline workers, sanitation crews, and winter storm recovery efforts. Council Member Rist highlighted Transit Equity Day and local tax assistance programs.

agenda_items.title: City Manager's Priority Items
agenda_items.discussion_summary: City Manager Ferguson presented priority items, recommending referring the Peregrine Technologies police operations platform contract back to staff and granting a continuance for the Creek Side mixed-use development zoning map change.

agenda_items.title: Refer Peregrine Technologies Contract Back to Staff
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The Council considered the Manager's priority item to refer the controversial Peregrine Technologies contract back to staff without further consideration, following extensive community feedback. Council members expressed support for the manager's recommendation.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Passed, 7-0 (Motion by Rist, Second by Cabayro, unanimous roll call vote).

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda Approval (Items 1, 2, 5, and 9 pulled)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The Council reviewed and approved the consent agenda, noting that items 1, 2, 5, and 9 were pulled for separate public comment or discussion.

agenda_items.title: Infrastructure Contracts & Paving Projects Public Hearing
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Public hearings and presentations were held for capital infrastructure contracts including street repairs, paving, and stormwater projects (Items 4 and 5). Public commenters raised equity concerns regarding capital investments in historically underserved neighborhoods like Hayti compared to gentrifying areas.

agenda_items.title: Consolidated Annexation - Curly Gardens & Utility Extension
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Public hearing and extensive deliberation on the consolidated annexation for Curly Gardens (Item 17). Property owners and representatives requested water line extension and annexation for 36 multi-family affordable housing units, while community members raised transparency concerns regarding future expansion into Orange County and urban growth boundary (UGB) implications. Ultimately, Council opted for a substitute motion to authorize a utility extension agreement without full annexation.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Passed substitute motion 6-0 authorizing utility extension agreement without full annexation.

agenda_items.title: DPAC Oversight Committee & Board Appointments
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The Council voted on board and committee appointments, including the Mayor's Council for Women and the Durham Performing Arts Center (DPAC) Oversight Committee appointments.

votes.item_title: Manager's Priority Item: Refer Peregrine Technologies contract back to staff
votes.discussion_detail: This manager's priority item involved referring the Peregrine Technologies contract back to staff following public feedback and review. Council members expressed appreciation for the manager's wisdom in referring the item back and for staff listening to council sentiments. Moved by Council Member Carl Rist and seconded by Mayor Pro Tem Javiera Caballero, the motion passed unanimously 7-0 on a voice vote.

votes.item_title: Substitute Motion for Curly Gardens: Authorize City Manager to enter into utility extension agreement without full annexation
votes.discussion_detail: Council considered an infill project case for Curly Gardens, where Council Member Cook proposed solely extending utilities rather than pursuing full annexation. Council Member Carl Rist agreed with the approach as a sound infill project with no traffic concerns, while staff provided context on policies and cost-benefit analysis. A substitute motion was framed by the city attorney and planning director to authorize the city manager to enter into a utility extension agreement with the Sidu Living Trust Trustee. Moved by Council Member Cook, the substitute motion passed unanimously 6-0.

votes.item_title: DPAC Oversight Committee Appointments (Rems and James Bullock)
votes.discussion_detail: The mayor brought forward committee appointments for the Durham Performing Arts Center oversight committee. The motion proposed appointing Rems representing arts and culture and James Bullock representing facility management, with terms expiring on March 1st, 2029. Properly moved and seconded, the appointments passed unanimously 6-0.

disagreements.issue: Curly Gardens Annexation vs Utility Extension
disagreements.summary: Discussion over whether to approve annexation for Curly Gardens Apartments or limit action to a utility extension agreement.
disagreements.side_a_position: Favor annexation and city water connection for the 36-unit affordable housing parcel.
side_a_arguments: Applicant and property owners (Bergman family / Curly Gardens Apartments) requested annexation to secure city water and replace an aging community well, citing maintenance costs and reliability concerns.
disagreements.side_b_position: Opposed full annexation to prevent UGB expansion, advocating instead for a limited utility extension agreement that provides water without annexing the parcel into the city.
side_b_arguments: Residents and public commenters raised concerns that annexation would crack the urban growth boundary (UGB) and serve as a stepping stone for a planned 84-unit expansion into Orange County.
disagreements.resolution: Adopted a substitute motion (6-0) to approve only the utility extension agreement rather than full annexation, avoiding expansion of the urban growth boundary (UGB) while granting water access.

meetings.executive_summary: The Durham City Council held a Work Session on January 22, 2026, which experienced initial technical and audio issues. The council reviewed the consent agenda (pulling items 4, 9, and 10), heard citizen comments on traffic safety (specifically on Guess Road) and police department technology, received updates and presentations, and discussed police department tools and public safety strategies.

agenda_items.title: Opening, Technical Issues, and Closed Session Report
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The meeting opened with a discussion on technical and audio issues that delayed the broadcast, prompting the Mayor and administration to explain a closed session held during the outage to handle legal matters.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda Readings and Pulls
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The Mayor read the consent agenda including committee appointments, contract approvals (street repairs, pavement preservation, utility locates), and grant acceptances. Items 4, 9, and 10 were pulled for separate discussion.

agenda_items.title: Citizens Matters and Public Comments
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Public comments addressed council decorum, transparency on COVID funds allocation, and traffic safety concerns on dangerous corridors like Guest Road, highlighting fatal traffic crashes and community advocacy.

agenda_items.title: Contract ST 342 Street Repairs and Repaving (2024 Bond)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council discussed Contract ST 342 for street repairs and repaving under the 2024 bond referendum, focusing on traffic calming integration, NACTO guidelines, and bike/pedestrian infrastructure.

agenda_items.title: Procurement of Police Operations Management Platform (Paragon Technologies)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Extensive deliberation and public/council debate on procuring a police operations management platform (Paragon Technologies) for the Durham Police Department real-time crime center, addressing privacy, surveillance concerns, and data sharing with federal agencies.

side_b_arguments: Public commenters and some council members expressed concerns regarding community surveillance, lack of trust in data privacy/federal agencies (like ICE), and the need to prioritize community safety, violence intervention, and restorative approaches over tech surveillance.
side_b_members: Council members (e.g., Councilwoman Burr/Baker referenced in debate)
disagreements.resolution: Item 10 was pulled from the consent agenda by the public for later discussion/review without a formal binding vote taken on the contract during this work session.

meetings.title: Durham City Council Work Session 1.22.2026 (Full Audio)
meetings.executive_summary: The Durham City Council held a work session covering winter ice storm preparedness, an unplanned mid-meeting closed session during a livestream audio outage, pulled consent items, and staff presentations on Falls Lake nutrient rules and the Digital Equity Plan. The sharpest debate centered on Agenda Item 10, a proposed $500,000 contract with Peregrine Technologies for a police Real-Time Crime Center data platform, which drew intense public opposition over surveillance and federal data access alongside strong support from residents and Mayor Leonardo Williams seeking tools to combat gun violence. Council moved Item 10 to the February 2 General Business Agenda and voted unanimously by voice vote to settle the remaining consent and public hearing items for the February 2 regular meeting.

agenda_items.title: Winter Weather and Ice Storm Preparedness Briefing
agenda_items.discussion_summary: City Manager Bo Ferguson requested taking Presentations 13 and 12 in reverse order and introduced department briefings on an approaching freezing rain and ice storm. Environmental and Street Services Director Marvin Williams outlined salt/sand treatment priorities across 25 outfitted trucks and potential solid waste collection delays, while Deputy City Manager Keith Chadwell covered emergency management activation, off-duty public safety staffing, and mass sheltering plans including limited pet capacity. Community Safety Director Ryan Smith detailed 24/7 shelter expansions for single adults, families, and medically vulnerable residents, HEART street outreach with partner agencies, and triage phone lines.

agenda_items.title: Attorney-Client Consultation Closed Session and Audio Outage Recess
agenda_items.discussion_summary: City Attorney Rehberg requested a closed session pursuant to N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(3) regarding two noticed, unfiled liability claims and potential city participation in an unfiled affirmative litigation action. When a broadcast audio failure required a technical reset at 00:40:55, Mayor Leonardo Williams recessed the open session to conduct the closed session immediately rather than waiting until the end of the meeting. Council reconvened in open session at 2:26 p.m. (01:26:35) once broadcast audio was restored.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda Reading (Items 1-11, 14-19) and Public Comments on Council Decorum, COVID Funds, and Traffic Safety
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Leonardo Williams read the upcoming February 2 agenda, noting Items 4, 9, and 10 were pulled for discussion while Item 8 (South Ellerbe Stormwater Project grant) and Public Hearings 14-19 were previewed. During Citizens' Matters, Jacqueline Wagstaff criticized Council decorum at the prior Monday meeting and Victoria Peterson requested an accounting of COVID/ARPA funding and interest earnings. Gregory Williams and grieving father Richard Davis (whose son Isaiah Davis was killed on Guess Road in November 2025) delivered a 300-signature petition urging immediate traffic-calming measures on Guess Road and state-maintained corridors.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Previewed / Items 4, 9, and 10 pulled for discussion

agenda_items.title: Contract ST-342: Street Repairs and Repaving 2026 (2024 Bond Referendum)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council Member Nate Baker pulled Item 4 to ask whether bond-funded street repaving incorporates traffic calming and NACTO design standards. Environmental and Street Services manager Clint Blackburn confirmed staff coordinates with Transportation to review all repaving streets against the Bike+Walk Plan, adding restriping, speed cushions, or speed humps where applicable. Baker critiqued auto-centric subdivision design as inducing speeding, while Council Member Carl Rist noted the ongoing joint City-County Bike+Walk Plan update will commit future CIP investments to 25 priority intersections, corridors, off-road links, and gaps.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Settled onto Consent Agenda for Feb 2 meeting

agenda_items.title: Second Amendment to Interlocal Cooperation Agreement with Durham Housing Authority for Security Equipment
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Pulled by Council Member Chelsea Cook and resident Victoria Peterson, who asked which public housing sites would receive equipment, this Cycle 3 Participatory Budgeting amendment provides additional contingency funds for cameras, bolt locks, door hardware, and lighting at Preiss-Steele Place and Cornwallis Road. Participatory Budgeting Manager Carmen Ortiz and Durham Housing Authority COO Ashanti Brown explained that delays stemmed from converting to upfront funding and project manager turnover, while cost increases reflected elevator infrastructure and server requirements. Cook questioned ongoing cellular and maintenance costs (which DHA will absorb), and Carl Rist praised the cross-jurisdictional collaboration.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Settled onto Consent Agenda for Feb 2 meeting

agenda_items.title: Contract with Peregrine Technologies, Inc. for DPD Operations Management Platform (Real-Time Crime Center)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Pulled by the public, this proposed ~$500,000 contract drew nine public commenters opposing it over surveillance expansion, predictive policing bias, third-party data aggregation, AI concerns, and potential ICE/federal subpoena exposure, while resident Victoria Peterson urged Council to approve cameras and policing tools to combat shootings in Black neighborhoods. Council Members Chelsea Cook, Nate Baker, Javiera Caballero, and Matt Kopac voiced opposition or serious reservations and called for strict guardrails or a privacy/surveillance commission, while Shanetta Burris and Mayor Leonardo Williams pressed colleagues for concrete solutions to gun violence rather than delaying action. Police Chief Patrice Andrews defended the platform as an investigative tool governed by strict audit policies rather than surveillance.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Moved to General Business Agenda (GBA) for Feb 2 meeting

agenda_items.title: Falls Lake Nutrient Strategy Rules Overview Presentation
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Environmental and Street Services staffer Michelle Woolfolk briefed Council on the state's upcoming 2027 rewrite of the 2011 Falls Lake nutrient rules, covering chlorophyll-a standards, strict 0.33 lb/acre/year total phosphorus targets for new development, offset credit scarcity, and the Upper Neuse River Basin Association's (UNRBA) investment-based compliance approach for existing development. Woolfolk warned that an impasse with the state over wastewater discharge caps amid regional growth may prompt UNRBA to petition the Environmental Management Commission with alternate rules as early as April, requiring quick Council action. Council Member Carl Rist highlighted Durham's $160,000 annual UNRBA investment, past wastewater nutrient reductions, and the risk of legislative intervention if 10 or more objections trigger General Assembly review.

agenda_items.title: Digital Equity Plan Update Presentation
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Digital Inclusion Program Manager Patrice Carroll and Digital Durham founder Laura Fogle presented progress on Durham's 2021 Digital Equity Plan, noting broadband adoption has reached 94.4% and device access 97% of county households alongside more than 12 new digital skills initiatives. Fogle highlighted Durham's consecutive National Digital Inclusion Association Visionary Trailblazer awards and an ARPA-funded digital navigator program launching February 25 with Durham Literacy Center, Stanford L. Warren Library, Student U, and Families Moving Forward. She flagged AI literacy, cybersecurity, and the end-of-2026 ARPA funding cliff as major upcoming challenges, drawing praise from Mayor Leonardo Williams, Carl Rist, and Chelsea Cook.

agenda_items.title: Motion to Settle the February 2, 2026 City Council Regular Meeting Agenda
agenda_items.discussion_summary: At the conclusion of the work session, City Manager Bo Ferguson summarized the settled agenda for the February 2 regular meeting: Consent Agenda Items 1 through 9 and 11, General Business Agenda (GBA) Item 10, and GBA Public Hearings Items 14 through 19. Council moved, seconded, and approved settling the agenda by unanimous voice vote.

votes.item_title: Settle the February 2, 2026 City Council Meeting Agenda (Consent Items 1-9 and 11; GBA Item 10; GBA Public Hearings Items 14-19)
votes.notes: Unanimous voice vote at end of work session placing Items 1-9 and 11 on Consent, Item 10 (Peregrine Technologies) on the General Business Agenda, and Items 14-19 on GBA Public Hearings for February 2, 2026.
votes.discussion_detail: Following all pulled-item discussions and presentations, City Manager Bo Ferguson read back the settled agenda assignments for the February 2, 2026 regular City Council meeting. Consent Agenda assignments included Items 1 through 9 and Item 11 (covering board nominations, minutes, street repaving and pavement contracts, the South Ellerbe Stormwater grant, the DHA participatory budgeting security amendment, and GoDurham ACCESS vehicles), while Item 10 (the Peregrine Technologies contract for DPD) was placed on the General Business Agenda per Chelsea Cook's request and Items 14 through 19 were scheduled as GBA public hearings. Mayor Leonardo Williams called for a motion to settle the agenda, which was moved, seconded, and approved without objection by voice vote. Mayor Williams also reminded colleagues of an 8:00 a.m. weather press conference the following morning prior to Council's retreat.

disagreements.meeting_title: Durham City Council Work Session 1.22.2026 (Full Audio)
disagreements.issue: Peregrine Technologies Real-Time Crime Center Software Contract (Item 10)
disagreements.summary: Council members sharply divided during the work session preview of a ~$500,000 contract with Peregrine Technologies for a Durham Police Department operations management platform, pitting concerns over surveillance, data aggregation, racial bias, and federal subpoena access against calls to equip police with investigative tools to curb violent and property crime.
disagreements.side_a_position: Oppose or withhold support for the Peregrine contract due to surveillance, data privacy, and federal subpoena risks unless strict governance guardrails are established first.
side_a_arguments: Aggregating municipal and third-party data into a centralized platform creates long-term surveillance risks and leaves data vulnerable to court-ordered federal or ICE subpoenas.

The joint Community Safety and Wellness Task Force did not recommend expanding police surveillance technology, whereas alternative investments in youth, housing, and school-based interventions are needed.
No new surveillance or data-integration technology should be deployed without first establishing a dedicated privacy/surveillance advisory commission and binding ordinance guardrails.
disagreements.side_b_position: Support the Peregrine platform or demand concrete, immediate tools for DPD to solve violent crimes and protect residents experiencing gun violence.
side_b_arguments: Residents in high-crime and Black neighborhoods are terrorized by shootings and homicides and deserve tangible tools to help DPD clear cases faster and deliver closure to victims' families.

Peregrine is an investigative case-management integration tool vetted by Technology Solutions rather than a surveillance system, and DPD maintains strict audit logs, termination penalties for misuse, and requires court-ordered subpoenas for federal access.
Repeatedly stalling anti-crime technology proposals with new commissions or task forces without offering viable alternatives fails communities demanding safety.
disagreements.resolution: Placed on the General Business Agenda (GBA) for formal debate and vote at the February 2, 2026 regular meeting (Carl Rist did not announce a position, requesting further information on how the platform interacts with the City-County violence reduction plan).

meetings.title: Durham City Council January 20, 2026
meetings.executive_summary: The Durham City Council held its regular meeting on January 20, 2026, presided over by Mayor Williams. The council approved contract amendments removing St. Joseph's Historic Foundation as fiscal agent for Hayti Promise CDC and authorizing grant agreement modifications, despite some council dissent. Following an extensive public hearing with significant resident opposition, the council debated and ultimately voted 6-1 to defeat the annexation and rezoning request for the Britmore residential development due to environmental, watershed, and infrastructure concerns.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Moment of Silence, Pledge of Allegiance, and Roll Call
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The City Council meeting was called to order by Mayor Williams, followed by a moment of silence and the Pledge of Allegiance. Roll call established the presence of all council members.

agenda_items.title: ARPA Subrecipient Grant Agreement Amendment - Hayti Promise CDC & St. Joseph's Historic Foundation
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Discussion and vote on the first amendment to the ARPA subrecipient grant agreement with Hayti Promise Community Development Corporation to remove St. Joseph's Historic Foundation as fiscal agent.

agenda_items.title: Subsequent Modifications to ARPA Grant Agreement & Fayetteville Street Corridor Implementation
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Discussion, public comments, and subsequent modifications to the amended ARPA subrecipient grant agreement with Hayti Promise CDC for the Fayetteville Street corridor neighborhood stabilization partnership implementation.

agenda_items.title: Oath of Office for Dr. Dorothy C. Brown (NC Symphony Board of Trustees)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: A unique oath of office was administered to Dr. Dorothy C. Brown, a Durham resident appointed by Governor Josh Stein to the North Carolina Symphony Society Incorporated Board of Trustees, followed by congratulatory remarks from the Mayor.

agenda_items.title: Consolidated Annexation and Zoning Map Change for Britmore
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Consolidated public hearing and board discussion regarding the Britmore annexation and zoning map change proposal (27 acres in southwest Durham). Extensive public comments were heard from residents, HOA representatives, and developers regarding environmental impacts on Jordan Lake, traffic, and housing density.

agenda_items.title: Council Member Announcements and MLK Day Reflections
agenda_items.discussion_summary: City council members shared announcements and reflections, including Martin Luther King Jr. Day marches, labor movement support, community service, winter weather preparations for unhoused residents, and budget season kick-off.

votes.item_title: First amendment to ARPA subrecipient grant agreement with Hayti Promise Community Development Corporation to remove St. Joseph's Historic Foundation as fiscal agent
votes.discussion_detail: The council considered the first amendment to the ARPA subrecipient grant agreement with Hayti Promise Community Development Corporation, which proposed removing St. Joseph's Historic Foundation as fiscal agent. Staff discussed ensuring that previously committed funds are honored while placing new commitments on hold pending further council clarification. Council members debated the appropriate timing and clarity around how funds were spent and allocated by the CDC. Following discussion, a motion was made and properly seconded to approve the contract amendment. The motion passed on a 6-1 vote, with Council Member Shanetta Burris casting the sole dissenting vote.

votes.item_title: Subsequent modifications to amended ARPA subrecipient grant agreement with Hayti Promise CDC
votes.discussion_detail: Building upon the previous item, the council considered authorizing the city manager to negotiate and make subsequent modifications to the amended ARPA subrecipient grant agreement with Hayti Promise Community Development Corporation, contingent upon total grant funds not exceeding $3,245,000. Public speakers during the meeting expressed appreciation for the comprehensive evaluation of items 12 and 13 together, while urging ongoing diligence, fidelity, and transparency regarding community investments for Hayti. Following brief discussion and motions, the vote was opened and closed. The motion passed by a 6-1 margin, with Council Member Shanetta Burris again voting in opposition.

votes.item_title: Ordinance annexing Britmore into the city of Durham and utility extension agreement with Tri Pointe Homes Holdings Inc.
votes.discussion_detail: The council reviewed an ordinance annexing Britmore (referenced as Brent Moore in the motion) into the city of Durham alongside a proposed utility extension agreement with Tri Pointe Homes Holdings Inc. Representatives and staff detailed extensive community outreach efforts, including virtual meetings and an on-site afternoon inspection addressing drainage and slope concerns raised by adjacent Montlair property owners. Council members deliberated on housing needs, environmental impacts, and broader equity considerations during the public hearing. After the public hearing was closed, a motion was made and seconded to adopt the annexation ordinance and authorize the utility extension agreement. The motion ultimately failed 1-6, with only Mayor Williams voting in favor of the measure.

disagreements.meeting_title: Durham City Council January 20, 2026
disagreements.issue: Britmore annexation and rezoning development proposal
disagreements.summary: Debate over whether the 27-acre Britmore residential annexation and rezoning project should be approved given comprehensive plan alignment versus severe environmental, watershed, and rural traffic impacts.
disagreements.side_a_position: Support approval of annexation and development agreement
side_a_arguments: Aligned with the comprehensive plan (mixed residential neighborhood)
Addresses housing supply shortage with mix of townhouses and single-family homes
Gravity sewer infrastructure and capacity already in place
Added proffer commitments including Energy Star rating, tree coverage, and funding donations
disagreements.side_b_position: Oppose annexation and development due to environmental and infrastructure impacts
side_b_arguments: Threatens Jordan Lake protected watershed, sensitive streams, and wildlife corridors
Inadequate rural road capacity and safety concerns at Ferington Mill and Chapel Hill roads
High market-rate pricing does not meet local lower-AMI affordable housing gaps
Planning Commission recommended removal from growth boundary
side_b_members: Local residents (Mark Patrick, Chris Peckham, Julie McClintock, etc.)
disagreements.resolution: Motion to approve annexation and utility extension failed 6-1 (with only Mayor Williams voting yes).

meetings.title: Durham City Council Work Session January 8, 2026
meetings.executive_summary: The Durham City Council held a work session on January 8, 2026, discussing community safety, CIP project timelines, and several pulled consent agenda items including ARPA subawards and bike lane designs. The primary focus of the meeting was an extensive staff presentation and council debate on the ongoing Unified Development Ordinance (UDO) update, covering housing density, complete streets, and environmental standards. Council members debated the effectiveness and strategy of density bonuses and affordability requirements within the new land use rules.

agenda_items.title: Announcements and Roll Call
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Meeting opened with roll call and council member announcements, including statements on community safety, federal policy, local events, and a tribute to retiring Police Chief Andrews.

agenda_items.title: Priority Items and Consent Agenda Pulls
agenda_items.discussion_summary: City Manager's office welcomed new management analyst Justin Rose; City Attorney and Clerk presented board/committee appointments and pull requests for the consent agenda.

agenda_items.title: Citizen Comment on CIP Stoplight Report
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Resident Dale McKielle presented public comments on the Capital Improvement Program (CIP) stoplight report, highlighting long delays in project development pipeline (design and right-of-way acquisition phases).

agenda_items.title: ARPA Subaward Agreement Amendments for St. Joseph Historic Foundation
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council discussed the first amendment to the ARPA state and local fiscal recovery funds subaward agreement with St. Joseph Historic Foundation (Hataí Promise CDC), reviewing expenditure tracking, federal deadlines, and interest accrual.

agenda_items.title: Reauthorization of Durham Bicycle and Pedestrian Advisory Commission (BPAC) Interlocal Agreement
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council discussed the interlocal agreement reauthorizing the Durham Bicycle and Pedestrian Advisory Commission (BPAC), addressing member application routing and commission recommendations.

agenda_items.title: Downtown Durham Bike Lanes Design Agreement Amendment
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council discussed the second amendment to master agreement with Kimley-Horn/MeandHunt for design of downtown Durham bike lanes, evaluating design enhancements, raised intersections, on-street parking impacts, and project timelines.

agenda_items.title: Unified Development Ordinance (UDO) Update Presentation and Discussion
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Planning staff (Bo Dinsky, Robin Schultz, Lisa Miller) presented an extensive update on the new Unified Development Ordinance (UDO) project, covering zoning districts, density bonuses, affordability incentives, transportation/complete streets, and environmental/tree canopy standards.

disagreements.meeting_title: Durham City Council Work Session January 8, 2026
disagreements.issue: Density bonuses and affordability requirements in the Unified Development Ordinance (UDO) update
disagreements.summary: Council members debated whether the proposed density and height bonuses coupled with affordability requirements would effectively incentivize development or if current mechanisms were overly restrictive.
disagreements.side_a_position: Argued that density and height bonuses must be strictly tied to affordable housing requirements to ensure equitable and just growth.
side_a_arguments: Density and height are precious commodities that should not be given away for free without securing meaningful affordable housing units.
Equitable growth around transit corridors requires tying density increases to deep affordability (e.g. 30-60% AMI).
disagreements.side_b_position: Expressed concern that overly rigid requirements on height/density bonuses fail in practice and hinder housing development.
side_b_arguments: Historical density and height bonuses in Durham have been underutilized and ineffective due to market realities and financing constraints.
Overly restrictive requirements risk halting housing production and ignoring practical economic realities.
disagreements.resolution: No formal vote was taken; council members agreed to continue the discussion and schedule further dedicated retreat time to examine the economic feasibility and rules of density bonuses.

meetings.title: Durham City Council January 5, 2026
meetings.executive_summary: The Durham City Council held its first meeting of 2026 on January 5, 2026. The council proclaimed Human Trafficking Prevention Month and celebrated the 25th anniversary of Together for Resilient Youth (TRI). Following a public hearing with extensive public comment on the Sage Brook townhouses annexation and rezoning project, the council debated infrastructure capacity, traffic, environmental buffers, and comprehensive plan alignment. Ultimately, the council approved the annexation and utility extension agreement, the zoning map amendment (both 4-3), and the consistency statement (7-0).

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Moment of Silence, Pledge of Allegiance, and Roll Call
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Leonardo Williams called the meeting to order, mentioning a 'mayor for a day' guest with a rare disease. Council held a moment of silence and recited the Pledge of Allegiance, followed by a roll call confirming all council members present.

agenda_items.title: Proclamation: Human Trafficking Prevention Month
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Pro Tempore Javier Cavierro read a proclamation recognizing January 2026 as Human Trafficking Prevention Month, accompanied by survivor advocate Reverend Cara Matthews from Shield NC who discussed grooming and myths surrounding human trafficking.

agenda_items.title: Announcements by Council Members
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council members shared brief New Year remarks, reflecting on family milestones, upcoming budget priorities, affordable housing challenges, and concerns regarding recent spikes in gun violence.

agenda_items.title: Proclamation: 25th Anniversary of Together for Resilient Youth (TRI)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Leonardo Williams presented a proclamation recognizing the 25th anniversary of Together for Resilient Youth (TRI) to Dr. Wanda Boon, highlighting their public health model, overdose prevention work, and community resilience efforts.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing: Sage Brook Townhouses Annexation and Rezoning
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Public hearing regarding the Annexation Ordinance, Zoning Map Amendment (from Rural/Suburban to Planned Development Residential), and Consistency Statement for Sage Brook Townhouses. Several residents spoke on traffic impacts, lack of EMS and medical infrastructure, stream buffers, and agricultural concerns, while the applicant's attorney responded regarding site design, impervious surfaces, and utility connectivity.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Passed across three separate votes (Annexation 4-3, Rezoning 4-3, Consistency Statement 7-0)

votes.item_title: Annexation Ordinance and Utility Extension Agreement for Sage Brook Townhouses
votes.notes: Motion to adopt an ordinance annexing Sage Brook townhouses into the city of Durham and authorizing the city manager to enter into a utility extension agreement with Capital City Homes LLC.
votes.discussion_detail: The Durham City Council considered an annexation ordinance and utility extension agreement for the Sage Brook Townhouses project with Capital City Homes LLC. The discussion touched upon broader themes of housing affordability for younger residents in Durham, housing abundance frameworks, and regional growth challenges. Council members debated the impacts of development, with specific mentions of traffic, local infrastructure, and farmland preservation in Southeast Durham leading to a commitment to review local growth patterns. The motion ultimately passed by a 4-3 vote, with Council Members Baker, Burris, and Cook voting in opposition.

votes.item_title: Zoning Map Amendment for Sage Brook Townhouses
votes.notes: Ordinance amending the UDO from Residential Rural (RR) / Jordan Watershed Overlay District B County to Planned Development Residential 6.9 (PDR-6.9) / Jordan Watershed Overlay District B City jurisdiction.
votes.discussion_detail: The council voted on a zoning map amendment for the Sage Brook Townhouses project to amend the unified development ordinance by taking property out of the county's residential suburban 20 Jordan Watershed Overlay District B jurisdiction and establishing it as planned development residential 6.905 within the city's jurisdiction. This zoning change supported the high-density residential townhouse development proposed by Capital City Homes LLC. The motion passed 4 to 3, with Council Members Baker, Burris, and Cook casting the dissenting votes.

votes.item_title: Consistency Statement for Sage Brook Townhouses
votes.notes: Required consistency statement pursuant to NC General Statutes Section 160D-605.
votes.discussion_detail: The council considered adopting the required statutory consistency statement under North Carolina General Statutes Section 160D-605 regarding the Sage Brook Townhouses zoning amendment and development plans. Unlike the contentious votes on the annexation and zoning map amendments, the consistency statement motion was adopted unanimously with a 7-0 vote.

disagreements.meeting_title: Durham City Council January 5, 2026
disagreements.issue: Sage Brook Townhouses Annexation and Rezoning (Non-Contiguous Development, Infrastructure, and Environmental Impact)
disagreements.summary: Debate over whether to approve the non-contiguous Sage Brook townhouses annexation and rezoning project, balancing housing need and tax base expansion against infrastructure strain and rural transition concerns.
disagreements.side_a_position: Supportive of approval for the annexation and rezoning project as a necessary infill/density step for housing and tax base expansion.
side_a_arguments: Aligns with the comprehensive plan's vision for density within the urban growth boundary
Provides 10 deed-restricted for-sale affordable housing units at 80% AMI
Developer pays for infrastructure costs rather than taxpayers
Expands the tax base to help fund municipal services and transit
disagreements.side_b_position: Opposed to approval due to infrastructure strain, non-contiguous annexation concerns, and consistency with rural preservation.
side_b_arguments: Inadequate infrastructure support (EMS, roads, medical facilities)
Creates a non-contiguous 'donut hole' annexation in a rural transition zone
Planning Commission recommended denial twice
Traffic and environmental/riparian buffer concerns raised by local residents and farmers
disagreements.resolution: Passed by 4-3 votes for annexation and rezoning, and 7-0 for the consistency statement.

meetings.title: Durham City Council Work Session December 16, 2025
meetings.executive_summary: The Durham City Council held its work session on December 16, 2025, presided over by Mayor Leo Williams. The council received presentations and held discussions on the Forever Home Durham affordable housing initiative progress and the downtown parking program overview. Additionally, the council approved the settlement of the agenda for the upcoming meeting.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Roll Call, and Announcements
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The mayor called the work session to order at 1:00 PM. Roll call was taken with all council members present except Mayor Pro Tem Cabayero who received an excused absence. Council members offered brief holiday remarks and appreciation for city staff.

agenda_items.title: City Manager, City Attorney, and Board/Committee Reports
agenda_items.discussion_summary: City Manager Bo Ferguson announced a holiday gift from his wife to council and staff and highlighted updated slides for Item 11 (Forever Home Durham). City Attorney reported no priority items. The Board and Committee report confirmed advisory board and commission appointments including Durham Cultural Advisory Board and Human Relations Commission.

agenda_items.title: Citizen Matters / Public Comment
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Public comments were delivered by multiple residents addressing free speech, council decorum, community activism, and recent actions regarding public access and civic participation at City Hall.

agenda_items.title: Update on Forever Home Durham
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff presented an update on the Forever Home Durham initiative, reviewing progress on creating and preserving affordable rental units, low-income household stabilization, and minority/women-owned business enterprise (MWBE) contracting goals. Council members discussed down payment assistance loan numbers, the eviction diversion program, affordability periods, and long-term housing levers.

agenda_items.title: Parking Program Overview
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff presented an overview of the downtown parking program, discussing parking utilization, deck vacancy, downtown worker discount programs, surface parking lots, and potential strategies like one-hour free parking and pricing adjustments to manage curb space demand.

agenda_items.title: Approval of the Settlement of the Agenda
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The city manager reviewed the settled agenda items including consent items 1-10 and GBA public hearing items 13 and 14 (with items 3, 4, and 5 pulled by Council Member Cook). A motion was made, seconded, and unanimously approved to settle the agenda.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Passed, Unanimous (Moved and properly seconded, all in favor)

meetings.title: Durham City Council December 15, 2025
meetings.executive_summary: The Durham City Council met on December 15, 2025, presided over by Mayor Leonardo Williams. The council adopted the Downtown Durham Blueprint 2035 Plan amending the Comprehensive Plan, approved zoning map changes and annexation for the Page Road Amendment (up to 15 townhomes), unanimously failed a non-contiguous conservation subdivision annexation/rezoning for Hamlin Reserve (2503 & 2523 Hamlin Road), and held a contentious public hearing on the 81.75-acre Lee Village Center compact suburban design rezoning (Z-23-00042), ultimately voting 6-1 to continue the public hearing and case to February 16, 2026.

agenda_items.title: Opening, Roll Call, and Meeting Protocol
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The meeting opened with a moment of silence, the Pledge of Allegiance, and a roll call. Mayor Leonardo Williams read a formal statement regarding decorum in council chambers and adherence to North Carolina General Statute 143-318.17 concerning meeting disruptions and removal procedures.

agenda_items.title: Ceremonial Proclamations
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The council presented two ceremonial proclamations: one recognizing the Salvation Army of Durham Holiday Impact Recognition Day (accepted by Major Angela and David Rivas), and another celebrating the 90th anniversary of the Durham Committee on Affairs of Black People (accepted by Senator Floyd McKissick and committee representatives).

agenda_items.title: Announcements by City Council
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council members shared announcements, congratulating community organizations, addressing recent tragic shootings globally and locally (including support for injured Durham Academy graduate Kendall Turner), highlighting white flag shelter bed expansions and homeless support services, and discussing community events.

agenda_items.title: CAPER Public Hearing & Housing Report
agenda_items.discussion_summary: City staff presented the Consolidated Annual Performance and Evaluation Report (CAPER) detailing HUD formula block grant funding (CDBG, HOME, HOPWA, ESG) and program achievements. Public commenters and council members discussed housing expenditures, unspent allocations, and homelessness supportive services.

agenda_items.title: Downtown Durham Blueprint 2035 Plan Comprehensive Plan Amendment
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Downtown Durham Incorporated (DDI) presented the Downtown Durham Blueprint 2035 plan, establishing a shared vision and targeted goals for downtown vibrancy, infrastructure, and growth. Following public comments, the council approved the comprehensive plan amendment.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Passed unanimously (7-0), moved by Council, seconded, vote closed at [01:30:59].

agenda_items.title: Page Road Amendment Zoning Map Change & Consistency Statement
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The council considered a zoning map change for 3404 Page Road (Z-25-00010) to amend the development plan across three parcels. Staff presented the application, the council held a public hearing, and subsequently approved the map change and consistency statement.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Passed unanimously (7-0); map change vote at [01:35:25], consistency statement vote at [01:35:45].

agenda_items.title: 3306 Page Road Annexation & Utility Extension Agreement
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The council reviewed a request for utility extension and annexation for 3306 Page Road to allow up to 15 townhouse units. Discussion covered utility agreements, connection terms, and monetary contributions before approval.

agenda_items.title: Hamlin Reserve Annexation & Rezoning
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The council reviewed the annexation and rezoning petition for Hamlin Reserve (2503 & 2523 Hamlin Road) involving 42.61 acres for a conservation subdivision. Council members debated consistency with the urban growth boundary and environmental considerations before voting against the annexation.

agenda_items.title: Lee Village Center Rezoning & Annexation (Z-23-00042) Continuance
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The council held a lengthy public hearing and deliberation on the Lee Village Center rezoning and annexation (Z-23-00042). Substantive debate centered around Traffic Impact Analysis (TIA) requirements and timing, transit-oriented development connectivity, and future bus stop placement, culminating in a motion to continue the case.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Passed (6-1, with Council Member Cook voting no), vote closed at [03:53:28] / [03:53:28] transcript timeline (~05:35:28).

votes.item_title: Downtown Durham Blueprint 2035 Plan Comprehensive Plan Amendment
votes.discussion_detail: Downtown Durham Incorporated President and CEO Nicole Thompson presented the Downtown Durham Blueprint 2035 plan to the City Council, requesting its adoption as an official city plan following a two-year engagement process involving over 2,300 people. The blueprint features a shared vision, seven targeted goals with deliberate strategies, and implementable actions to support continued growth and vibrancy while preserving downtown's unique character. Following a public hearing with one public speaker, the council entertained a motion to adopt a resolution amending the Durham Comprehensive Plan, which passed unanimously with a 7-0 vote.

votes.item_title: Page Road Amendment Zoning Map Change (3404 Page Road / Z-25-00010)
votes.discussion_detail: Pamela Porter of TMTLA Associates proposed amending an existing graphic development plan (Z-17-00031) on three parcels located at 0, 1000, and 1002 Oak Mill Drive to allow an additional external access point on the eastern portion adjacent to 3306 Page Road. The current Planned Development Residential 5.788 zoning designation remained unchanged, and the amendment was graphically depicted on sheet three of attachment D. Staff and applicant presented the request during a public hearing, after which the council voted to adopt the ordinance and consistency statement, passing both unanimously with a 7-0 vote.

votes.item_title: Page Road Amendment Consistency Statement
votes.discussion_detail: Following the zoning map change presentation and public hearing for the 3404 Page Road amendment, the council considered adopting a consistency statement as required by North Carolina General Statute Section 160D-605. The motion was properly moved and seconded, and the clerk opened the vote. The consistency statement passed unanimously with a 7-0 vote.

votes.item_title: 3306 Page Road Annexation & Utility Extension Agreement
votes.discussion_detail: Pamela Porter of TMTLA Associates and Jeff Palmer of Shenandoah Homes requested a utility extension agreement, voluntary annexation, and initial zoning map change for a 1.82-acre parcel at 3306 Page Road from Residential Rural to Planned Development Residential 8.876 to allow up to 15 townhouse units as a contiguous expansion of the Page Oaks neighborhood. The applicant addressed council questions regarding pedestrian and cyclist access, confirming a commitment to build a 10-foot shared path connecting the terminus of Oak Mill Drive to the path on Page Road without vehicular connection. After addressing a brief procedural mix-up in motion ordering, the council adopted the annexation ordinance, utility extension agreement, and required consistency statement, all passing unanimously with a 7-0 vote.

votes.item_title: Hamlin Reserve Annexation & Rezoning (2503 & 2523 Hamlin Road)
votes.discussion_detail: The council considered an annexation and rezoning request for Hamlin Reserve (2503 and 2523 Hamlin Road). Extensive discussion focused on whether approving the conservation-subdivision model outside the urban growth boundary would set a problematic precedent for future developments and undermine growth boundary enforcement, with council members drawing comparisons to the unanimously rejected Mariah Ridge case. Concerns were also raised regarding the developer, KB Homes, and their alleged inaction regarding ruined wells down on Junction Road. Citing consistency and the importance of adhering to the urban growth boundary, all council members voted against the motion. The motion failed unanimously with a 0-7 vote, with Nays recorded from Mayor Williams, Mayor Pro Tem Caballero, and Council Members Baker, Burris, Cook, Copack, and Rist.

votes.item_title: Lee Village Center Rezoning & Annexation (Z-23-00042) Continuance
votes.discussion_detail: The council considered a motion to keep the public hearing open and continue the rezoning and annexation case for the Lee Village Center (Z-23-00042) until February 16, 2026. Discussion centered around outstanding questions regarding traffic impact analyses (TIA), parkland priorities, mix of uses, and neighborhood street connectivity. Members noted that transit infrastructure like bus shelters, pads, and pullouts would be implemented at the site plan phase per compact urban design standards and zoning commitments. Despite resident opposition regarding connectivity and concerns about the application's details, several members expressed willingness to grant a continuance to give the new council time to address questions. The motion passed 6-1, with Council Member Cook voting in opposition.

disagreements.meeting_title: Durham City Council December 15, 2025
disagreements.issue: Traffic Impact Analysis (TIA) requirement and timing for large rezoning (Lee Village Center, Z-23-00042)
disagreements.summary: Debate over whether a Traffic Impact Analysis (TIA) was legally mandated prior to zoning approval for the 81.75-acre Lee Village Center project, or whether deferring granular TIAs to the site plan stage was appropriate.
disagreements.side_a_position: Require TIA immediately or send back to planning department; oppose voting/continuing without strict statutory compliance.
side_a_arguments: A TIA is strictly required by UDO section 3.3 at the time of zoning change (word 'shall' is mandatory); voting without it is a dereliction of duty.
disagreements.side_b_position: Accept planning director's determination; perform granular TIAs at each phase of site plan approval while continuing the public hearing to Feb 16, 2026 to resolve park and use clarity.
side_b_arguments: Under 160D-405, administrative appeal window on planning director's TIA decision has passed; due to large phased buildout (1,667–2,294 units over 10-20 years) and form-based compact suburban design, scoping an overall TIA violates rational nexus/rough proportionality, making site-plan level TIAs more rigorous and appropriate.
side_b_members: Applicant legal counsel, Planning Director, Mayor Williams, and majority of Council
disagreements.resolution: Motion to continue the public hearing and case to February 16, 2026 passed 6-1 (Council Member Cook voted against continuing/passing because she argued a TIA is legally mandated prior to zoning approval).

meetings.title: Durham City Council Work Session December 4, 2025
meetings.executive_summary: The Durham City Council convened for a Work Session on December 4, 2025, presided over by Mayor Williams. The council discussed administrative consent items, heard presentations on the 505 West Chapel Hill Street redevelopment options (including preservation via Preservation North Carolina), reviewed the 2025 third quarter crime report, and examined the FY 2025-2026 first quarter financial report. Several consent items were pulled for separate discussion, and Item 10 (redevelopment loan agreement with Durham Housing Authority) was referred back to staff upon request.

agenda_items.title: Council Announcements, Roll Call, and Meeting Decorum
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Williams called the meeting to order and roll call was conducted. Council members shared announcements including participatory budgeting updates, the Carolina Theater centennial campaign, and local sports events. Mayor Williams addressed decorum following disruptions at a prior meeting and announced new time limits for council member discussions.

agenda_items.title: City Manager & City Attorney Priority Updates
agenda_items.discussion_summary: City Manager announced winter weather monitoring, introduced Starleta Tanner as the new permanent director of Community Partnerships and Engagement, and noted that DHA requested item 10 be referred back to staff. The City Attorney requested a closed session for attorney-client consultation on as-yet-unfiled litigation.

agenda_items.title: Board and Committee Appointments Report
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The City Clerk presented board and committee appointments, including Frederica Cadeno for the Participatory Budgeting Steering Committee (youth category) and Doug Pender for the Durham Convention and Visitors Bureau Discover Durham appointment.

agenda_items.title: Public Comments: Swing Pals Program
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Doug Hodges, founder and executive director of Swing Pals, spoke during Citizens Matter about the nonprofit providing mindfulness and golf resilience coaching for underserved youth in Durham public schools and thanked the council for supporting Hillendale Golf Course.

agenda_items.title: Hiring Practices Performance Audit (November 2025)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Audit Services Director Germaine presented a performance audit on hiring practices, discussing timelines, application processes, and recommendations to streamline hiring. HR manager Jim O'Donnell answered questions regarding applicant onboarding and job application requirements.

agenda_items.title: Tennis Court Lighting Purchase Contracts (Whipperwill Park & Rock Quarry Park)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council discussed purchase contracts for tennis court lighting at Whipperwill Park and Rock Quarry Park with Musco Sports Lighting LLC, focusing on Dark Sky compliance, lighting fixtures, spillover reduction, and fixture design standards.

agenda_items.title: Proposed Lease with Durham Regional Association of Realtors at 4238 University Drive
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council discussed a proposed lease agreement with the Durham Regional Association of Realtors Incorporated at 4238 University Drive, reviewing lease terms, property usage, and real estate department details.

agenda_items.title: Consolidated Annexation: Lee Village Center
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council reviewed the consolidated annexation for Lee Village Center (and related zoning/development items), discussing traffic impact analysis (TIA) requirements, UDO compliance, density thresholds, and planning commission recommendations.

agenda_items.title: Update on Redevelopment of 505 West Chapel Hill Street
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Extensive presentation and deliberation on redevelopment scenarios for the 505 West Chapel Hill Street site (Home Security Life Insurance Building). Topics included building preservation vs. demolition, estimated rehab costs ($25-30M), historic preservation covenants with Preservation North Carolina, interim activation open space, and affordable housing financing constraints (9% LIITC and parking requirements).

agenda_items.title: 2025 Third Quarter Crime Report
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Durham Police Department presented the 2025 third quarter crime report, reviewing violent crime trends through September, homicides (36 to date), domestic incidents, robberies, firearm involvement, and aggravated assaults.

agenda_items.title: Fiscal Year 2025-2026 First Quarter Financial Report
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff presented the FY 2025-2026 first quarter financial report, discussing quarterly stoplight reports, budget performance, CIP reporting, and departmental financial tracking.

agenda_items.title: Closed Session: Attorney-Client Consultation on As-Yet-Unfiled Litigation
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Pursuant to NC General Statute 143-318.11(a)(3), the city attorney requested and council voted to enter closed session for attorney-client consultation to discuss as-yet-unfiled litigation.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Approved unanimously (Motion by Council Member Cook)
